What the exemplars do (target/p2/w4/exemplars.txt; V8 c8b70908, SM 6bb81100, JSC 26027804, each
checked at its main of 2026-11-04, where the cited code holds; 1,370 ranges checked, 0 problems):
- A1: each first tier records value feedback on every execution, before an optimizing tier
  exists: V8's Ignition in a byte of the bytecode (V8 interpreter-generator.cc:991-1012), SM's
  Baseline Interpreter by attaching stubs (SM jit/JitScript.h:317-340), JSC's LLInt in its arith
  and value profiles (JSC LowLevelInterpreter64.asm:1236-1290). TRust's first tier, the
  tree-walker, records nothing.
- A2: in the baseline, V8's Sparkplug+ calls a typed stub chosen from that byte, whose fast path
  writes nothing; a type miss merges the byte and repatches the call
  (V8 baseline-compiler.cc:1258-1299; V8 runtime-compiler.cc:158-198). JSC's baseline writes arith
  result bits on its double paths only (JSC ArithProfile.cpp:74-93). SM's stubs count their
  entries (SM jit/BaselineCacheIRCompiler.cpp:233-236), and JSC's value profiles store on every
  baseline execution (JSC JITInlines.h:311-319).
- A3: int32-ness is a tag in all three; an integral double is a double (V8 records kNumber,
  V8 binary-op-assembler.cc:572-581; JSC's SpecAnyIntAsDouble, JSC SpeculatedType.cpp:637-648).
  Only V8 tests a double by value, for kAdditiveSafeInteger
  (V8 code-stub-assembler.cc:7626-7661).
- A4: V8 records comparisons in the same byte (V8 globals.h:2663-2703); JSC records none and
  types them from their operands' predictions (JSC DFGFixupPhase.cpp:824-904). None records branch
  directions (V8 interpreter-generator.cc:1414-1432; JSC LowLevelInterpreter64.asm:2263-2275).
- A5: calls: V8 keeps a weak target, a closure literal's FeedbackCell or the megamorphic symbol,
  with a count on every call (V8 ic-callable.tq:91-168); SM a function, then a script, then
  "scripted" stubs, whose entry count drives trial inlining (SM jit/CacheIR.cpp:6607-6624;
  SM jit/TrialInlining.cpp:779-784); JSC up to 8 callees, then a virtual call
  (JSC Repatch.cpp:171-184).
- A6: property feedback changes on misses only, up to 4 maps in V8 (then homomorphic) and 6 stubs
  in SM (V8 ic.cc:569-648; SM jit/ICState.h:26-34). Elements: V8's kinds live in the map and its
  handlers' load and store modes (V8 map.h:368-382; V8 globals.h:3131-3168); SM has none, a shape
  and a packed bit (SM jit/CacheIR.cpp:3018-3065); JSC's access paths store the last StructureID
  on every execution (JSC LowLevelInterpreter64.asm:2022-2029).
- A7: V8 removed allocation-site pretenuring on 2026-10-27 (commit 21e810452ab9; before it, 100
  mementos and a survival ratio of 0.80, V8 pretenuring-handler.cc@9e976bfb:28-69); its sites
  keep elements kinds and boilerplates, made at a literal's second execution
  (V8 runtime-literals.cc:711-734). SM keeps a site word in every nursery cell and counts
  promotions at minor collections, tenuring at 0.9 over more than 200 allocations
  (SM gc/Heap.h:589-602; SM gc/Pretenuring.cpp:175-245, 270-352). JSC, non-moving with sticky marks
  like TRust, counts no survival and never pretenured (JSC MarkedSpace.cpp:404-433).
- A8: inlined code reads its callee's own feedback: V8's (vector, slot)
  (V8 feedback-source.h:15-39), SM's per-call-site ICScript (SM jit/TrialInlining.cpp:809-861),
  JSC's CodeOrigin, whose baseline CodeBlock owns the profiles (JSC InlineCallFrame.h:196-205);
  JSC's exits record FrequentExitSite by bytecode index (JSC DFGOSRExitBase.cpp:38-60).
- A9: dependencies are recorded during compilation and checked at install: V8's
  CompilationDependencies into per-object DependentCode (V8 compilation-dependencies.cc:1450-1510),
  SM's fuses (SM jit/WarpOracle.cpp:1236-1283), JSC's DesiredWatchpoints into three-state
  watchpoint sets, whose firing jettisons the code and unlinks its incoming calls
  (JSC DFGPlan.cpp:553-600; JSC CodeBlock.cpp:2431-2433).
- A10: missing feedback is an exit, megamorphic feedback is not: V8's "insufficient type
  feedback" deopt (V8 js-type-hint-lowering.cc:774-803; V8 js-heap-broker.cc:579-584), SM's
  MBail(FirstExecution) for a never-run IC (SM jit/WarpOracle.cpp:1074-1096), JSC's ForceOSRExit
  for an empty prediction (JSC DFGByteCodeParser.cpp:1319-1330).
- A11: none reports coverage of executed operations. JSC gates DFG tier-up on 75% of a
  function's value profiles being live, after up to 5 delays (JSC CodeBlock.cpp:3049-3058;
  JSC OptionsList.h:401-404).
- A12: V8 allocates a function's vector once it has executed 8 times its bytecode length
  (V8 flag-definitions.h:1110-1111); SM makes its ICScript at a warm-up count of 10 and drops it
  with the JIT code at a major collection (SM jit/BaselineJIT.cpp:631-644; SM gc/GC.cpp:3006-3036).

Design:
1. Value classes, always on, on the VM's and miss paths only (the plan's rule; A2's Sparkplug+ and
   JSC's baseline arith):
   - For arithmetic, unary, update and comparison (relational and equality) operations: three
     ValueClass sets (operand 0, operand 1, result) in one u32, ORed and stored only on change.
     The VM writes it on every execution; generated code where its in-line path misses (the
     census's patch, 537ec5f1, measured as is).
   - The record is a u32 a pc in an array the chunk makes at its first record: only 7-76% of the
     compiled chunks recorded anything in the census's JIT runs (target/p2/w4/census/). A write
     indexes it by pc, with no search: today's detailed vector searches its sites on every write
     (feedback.rs:1247-1278). The patch's array, made with each chunk, is the measured form.
   - The in-line set is part of the schema: each template publishes the classes it takes without
     a record (Number for arithmetic and relational comparison, int32 for `%`, the element
     templates' word and typed-array receivers with index keys). P3 reads rule U: the record plus
     the in-line set. It is safe by construction, and exact at the coarse grain for 89.7-100% of
     arithmetic executions on 19 of 20 workloads.
   - int32: the record's int32 bit is a hint, written only by the VM and misses. P3 speculates
     int32 where the record has no double and the use wants an integer (bit operations, indices,
     int32 element stores), f64 elsewhere: a Number is already its f64 word, so f64 arithmetic
     needs no boxing [inference]. A wrong int32 speculation is an exit, which Phase 3's exit
     profile turns into a recompile (Carried to Phase 3).
   - Equality is not recorded in line (JSC records no comparison, A4). P3 lowers it as the
     baseline does, by tag, and narrows it from its operands' producers.
   - Cheaper records than the patch's: the element record is taken in fast_get_elem and
     fast_set_elem, which borrow the receiver and test its kind and the key anyway (chai's 15.8M
     element records then cost a few instructions each [inference]); a word already Generic is
     not reclassified.
2. Elements kinds: the element record above, from the word block's kind bits (W2c's byte,
   word_block.rs:35-71), on the VM's and miss paths. Its known gap: an in-line hit tells an
   Array from a typed array only if a miss or the VM ran there. P3 keeps the baseline's two-way
   dispatch where the record is empty, and reads the array's kind bits at run time as the
   templates do. Recording in line would cost a load, a test and a branch at every element
   access; the census's 14.6% of zlib's operations are element accesses, so it stays out of W4.
3. Megamorphic and generic states:
   - Named sites: a per-site state byte beside its 4 ways, set by a fill that is refused (an
     uncacheable receiver, chai's proxies [inference]) or that evicts a live way, as CallSite
     counts evictions in an epoch (bytecode.rs:1350-1366). It marks a site generic, which P3
     lowers to the stub cache's probe (A10: megamorphic feedback is usable). The fill path only.
   - Calls: CallSite's megamorphic state (W3 item 7) as is. The per-way count stays parked
     (e854636e) until P3's inliner reads it: P3's hotness can come from the callee's jit_runs.
4. The read API: crate::feedback::read, for a chunk and a baseline pc, returning one typed view a
   kind:
   - values: the three class sets with the in-line set applied (rule U), and whether a record
     exists;
   - element: receiver families, the Array facts, key kinds, out of bounds;
   - named: each way's receiver shape, holder shape, depth, slot location and kind (data,
     accessor, absent, creation), and the generic mark;
   - call and construct: the state (empty, monomorphic, polymorphic, megamorphic) and each way's
     target: the callee cell, its function literal (the FeedbackCell's role, as V8's one literal
     with many closures), the builtin id, the native entry, the class;
   - allocation: the image or template if made, the constructor's class, the site's survival
     record (design 6).
   It allocates nothing and interns nothing: P3 runs in the process that made the shapes. The
   versioned envelope and refresh_current_layout_feedback (bytecode.rs:6243) remain the
   diagnostics' adapters, built on the same views. The detailed vector stays a diagnostic.
5. The schema document, tracked as crates/trust-js/src/feedback-schema.txt (AGENTS.md ignores
   Markdown workfiles), and feedback.rs's header pointing at it. It holds:
   - the numeric encodings, append-only within a version: OperationKind (with Comparison, 11),
     ObservationKind, ValueClass, ObservationState, roles;
   - each kind's record word: the value-class layout, the element bits, the named state byte;
   - each template's in-line set, the rule-U reading, and that a record never shrinks;
   - the read API's fields, which are exact and which hints (int32), and when a view goes stale
     (call-cache epochs, shapes);
   - the pc map (design 7) and site identity;
   - the coverage and precision definitions (design 8) and the census tool that measures them.
6. Allocation-site records and survival:
   - A site record a pc for MakeObject, MakeArray, MakeArrayLiteral, NewObject, NewArray,
     MakeClosure, MakeRegExp and New, plus one "built-in" record a call site: allocations,
     survivors and their bytes.
   - The object's cell carries its site's 16-bit index in the two padding bytes after
     NamedEntries' len_slot [inference from the fields' sizes, to be confirmed with
     -Zprint-type-sizes]. The allocation helpers and the in-line allocation store it and increment
     the site's count, as SM's Baseline does in machine code (SM jit/MacroAssembler.cpp:708-737;
     SM gc/Nursery-inl.h:213-247): about 5 instructions an in-line allocation [inference], Splay's
     800K in-line allocations about 0.3% of its run. A minor collection's marking reads the index
     of each young object it marks and increments the survivors (SM gc/Tenuring.cpp:945-958).
   - What the records serve: P3's allocation sinking (sites that die young: PdfJS's and chai's
     94-99% of allocations), and the class and slack decisions W2d step 3e makes per constructor.
     Pretenuring is not W4's: V8 removed it and JSC never had it (A7), and in a non-moving heap it
     saves a minor collection's mark of a survivor, not a copy, while its initializing stores
     then need their cards. Splay (24-28% of its run in minor collections, 97.8% survival) is
     where an experiment would pay; it waits for the records and an owner's decision.
7. Inlined and recompiled pcs mapped to their baseline sites (A8's form):
   - The inliner's splice records, for each spliced operation, the callee's chunk and pc; the
     transformed chunk keeps the map (one u32 a pc and the callee chunks' list) beside its inline
     sites (stack_trace.rs:86-97, bytecode.rs:9107).
   - A transformed chunk's miss paths write the always-on record through the map into the
     baseline site's word, so a callee's sites see what its inlined copies saw (Vue's 98%). Its
     caches stay its own (they are its speed); the read API merges a transformed site's ways with
     its baseline site's.
   - FeedbackVector::unbound goes (feedback.rs:735-741): the map makes the "coincidentally equal
     pc" it guards against impossible.
   - P3's own exits (Phase 3) record by baseline pc through the same map, as JSC's FrequentExitSite
     does (A8).
8. Coverage and precision as standing metrics:
   - Coverage: the share of the speculation kinds' executed operations whose site P3 can compile
     without an exit for missing feedback (V8's sense, A10). Precision: the share whose feedback,
     read by rule U, names exactly the coarse classes the operation saw.
   - Measured by the census's two runs, made a tracked diagnostic under the
     architecture-diagnostics feature, as the allocation-site probes are (DIAGNOSTICS.md), so that
     ordinary builds pay nothing: TRUST_JS_FEEDBACK_CENSUS=<path> (the VM loop's counts and full
     records in a --tier=bytecode run; the production state in the --tier=jit run) and
     scripts/feedback-census.py, which joins them and prints both metrics by kind. Reported at
     every stage exit beside instruction counts, from W4's exit on.
   - JSC's live-profile share (A11) is a per-function gate, not a measure of executed operations;
     P3 may add it at its tier-up.
9. Pilot C and the dependency registry:
   - Pilot C's proof is shapes keyed by attributes, landed by W2d steps 1-2: reads trust the shape
     where a way proves data. What remains is writability: a store's way cannot prove it, because
     a read's fill and a store's share one cache (W2d's record, item 2), so generated stores
     test the attribute byte (guard_slot_writable_data, jit_storage.rs:268). Finishing Pilot C:
     a store site's fill admits only a writable data property, and a read site's fill never reaches
     a store site's ways, as the global name cache already does (c9d8babe); the three-instruction
     test then goes from the stores, and the read API reports writability as proven.
   - The dependency registry, JSC's form (A9): a watchpoint set (clear, watched, invalidated)
     on each fact compiled code may assume: a shape with no transitions out, a prototype's
     shape, a protector (array_prototypes_unshadowed, interpreter.rs:9820), a global binding's
     constancy, an allocation site's decision. A compilation collects the sets it relies on and
     installs itself in them at the end, failing if one has fired; firing marks its codes
     invalid and unlinks their callers' call caches (Carried to Phase 3 names this as the home of
     JSC's incoming-call unlinking). PROTO_EPOCH and CALL_IC_EPOCH (value.rs:8168,
     bytecode.rs:1206) stay for the baseline's caches.
   - W4 builds the registry with its first producers (protectors, prototype shapes) and a test
     consumer; P3 is its first real one.

Order (each step measured on its own, as the plan's stages):
1. The schema document and feedback.rs's header (no code).
2. The census tool as a tracked diagnostic (TRUST_JS_FEEDBACK_CENSUS and the script), so every
   later step reports coverage and precision.
3. The value-class record (design 1), with the in-line sets in the schema, ARM64 and x86-64 miss
   paths.
4. The element record (design 2), inside the receiver reads the miss paths make.
5. Named sites' generic mark (design 3).
6. The read API (design 4), with its tests against the census's records.
7. The pc map and write-through for inlined chunks (design 7).
8. Allocation-site records and survival counting (design 6), with the header's site index.
9. Pilot C's store writability (design 9), with dump checks: store templates change.
10. The dependency registry (design 9).
Region admission's step 5 (speculation from W4's value classes) follows step 6.

Change surface:
- feedback.rs (the record, the read API, the schema's encodings), a new
  crates/trust-js/src/feedback-schema.txt.
- bytecode.rs: the chunk's record; the VM's arithmetic, comparison and element paths
  (bin_num, bin_i32, bin_cmp and the unary and update paths, bytecode.rs:21617-21756; the element
  paths, 26238-26340); jit_exec's operations, jit_add_strings and jit_strict_eq (24066-24260); the
  allocation helpers; the inliner's splice (the pc map).
- interpreter.rs: fast_get_elem and fast_set_elem (the element record), ic_insert (the generic
  mark).
- value.rs and gc_core.rs: the header's site index; the minor collection's marking (survivors).
- jit.rs, jit_alloc.rs, jit_x64_alloc.rs: in-line allocation's site-index store; the store
  templates' writability test (Pilot C).
- The census tool: the VM loop's count (bytecode.rs:18155) and a dump at exit; a script.
- Tests: the record's writes per path (VM, each miss helper; never an in-line hit), rule U against
  the full record on a test program, the pc map under inlining, survival counts across minor and
  major collections, the registry's install-time check and firing.

Risks:
- x86-64 was not measured. Its backend has in-line comparisons, equality and bit operations but
  no in-line f64 Add, Sub, Mul or Div: they take jit_exec on every execution (jit_x64.rs:1048-1099),
  so the record runs there every time. Measure on zombie before landing step 3; if it is over
  budget, x86-64 records the tag's coarse class only, or gets the f64 templates first.
- A record written in line by mistake costs every execution: a test runs each template's hit
  and checks the record unchanged.
- A template whose in-line set grows without the schema saying so makes rule U wrong. The census
  tool's "complete" column (99.8-100% today) is its check, at every stage exit.
- int32 hints from one-iteration samples drift (sustained, NavierStokes, Box2D). P3 must treat
  them as hints guarded by exits, not as proofs.
- The header's site index must stay out of the way of W2d's layout; if the padding is not free,
  the index costs a word, which the census then has to price.
- Equality and element receivers stay imprecise (precision 67.2-99.5%). Raising them needs records
  on in-line paths or a recording warm-up; either is P3's call, priced by this census's numbers.

Exit (proposed):
- The record on by default at <= 2% instructions on the acceptance set (the plan's), on ARM64 and
  on x86-64 (zombie). The patch measured 0.00-1.66% on ARM64 (Gameboy 1.66%, chai 1.62%, PdfJS
  1.46%), before design 1's cheaper element record.
- Coverage >= 95% on every workload, as the census tool measures it (the plan's number; the
  census gives 99.6-100.0% for W4's design, against 0.0-83.1% today). The plan's "usable
  feedback" can mean usable or right; this note measures both, and the 95% applies to usable.
- Precision reported beside it, by kind, with no workload below this census's (67.2-99.5%), so a
  change that loses records shows. A precision target belongs to P3, whose speculation sets the
  grain.
- The detailed vector stays a diagnostic.
Why change the plan's exit: under the in-line convention every executed site whose in-line path
ran is usable, so coverage meets 95% by construction and stops measuring how good the feedback
is. Precision does, and it is where the remaining gaps are (equality, element receivers, int32).

Decided (mine, reported to the owner; the exemplars' answers taken):
1. No recording warm-up. A VM warm-up is a compile-policy change (the counts moved -6.3% to
   +4.1% for reasons other than feedback), and it belongs with the tier threshold, which the
   owner has open ("The phase exit's gap, measured"); W4 records on VM and miss paths only.
2. No pretenuring in P2: V8 removed allocation-site pretenuring (2026-10-27) and JSC never had
   it. Step 8 (allocation-site records and survival counting) then has no consumer in P2 (the
   literals' boilerplates are W2e's images, slack tracking is W2d's per constructor), and moves to
   P3 with this census's survival tables.
3. No equality feedback: P3 types equality from its operands, as JSC does.

### Export accessors' binding proof read in place (record, 2026-11-04)

A phase-exit item ("The phase exit's gap, measured": Vue's Interp::try_binding_getter, 5.0% of
its instructions). The bundler's export accessors (`get: () => binding`) read their binding
through a cached proof of the scope chain (property_read.rs), which try_binding_getter took out
of the getter's sidecar and set back on every call: two take-and-set pairs of the 48-byte proof,
about half of the function's instructions (perf annotate). The probe runs no JavaScript and
writes no cache, so UserCallable::binding_getter_proof borrows the proof in place; a stale proof
is replaced after the reference ends (f0810c79, rebased onto main as the commit before this
record).

### W2g step 1: Proxy state in the object (record, 2026-11-04)

Commits, from main 3e7d856f, on p2-w2g-proxy (an agent's; rebased onto main dffe8831 as e7aed168,
5249c358, d3843a2e and 710191fd, with a31509fe correcting step 3's comment, which named the
sentinel this series removes; the measurements below name the series as written, then the rebased
one against dffe8831):
- c26c97b7: a Proxy's target and handler in its object. ObjectKind::Proxy(PayloadBox<ProxyData>)
  holds the target, the handler (null once revoked) and whether the target was callable. The
  object's trace reports the payload cell and its two edges, and revocation nulls the handler
  through the object's mutable borrow, which sets its card. is_callable gains the Proxy tag and
  the `Native(proxy_uncallable)` kind goes; the call dispatch's proxy test is a test of the tag,
  and every other reader (proxy_pair, the [[Get]], [[Set]], HasProperty and delete walks, the
  construct dispatch, GetFunctionRealm, the ordinary-get check, for-in, the feedback kinds,
  Engine::is_proxy_value) tests the kind. IsConstructor stays the flag bit the creation sets,
  which value_is_constructor now reads instead of recursing into the target. The table, the pin,
  its ClientRecords record, the conditional edge, the eviction and the cross-interpreter routing
  go, with with_metadata_table (revocation was its only use) and call_inner's and
  construct_inner's proxy guards before callable_home (which finds no [[Realm]] for the kind).
- 9a76763f: the realm-wide inline_ic_safe latch goes. The JIT's in-line `instanceof` walk and its
  interpreter counterpart (instanceof_ic) test each holder for a proxy; OrdinaryHasInstance's walk
  shares the interpreter's (prototype_chain_has), which stops at the first proxy, from which the
  observable walk goes on. JitCtx keeps its slot [32], unused (`reserved`), so that the fixed
  offsets after it stay.
- 93b6151e: the walk in six instructions a hop, as before it tested anything (9a76763f's took
  nine): KIND_PROXY_TAG is 32, the one tag with bit 5 set, so a TBNZ tells a proxy after the
  holder's tag and prototype loads, whose offsets from the cell fold in, and the loop branches
  back while the prototype is not the target. The entry loses the latch's three instructions.
- cedee510: the call and construct dispatch take the callee's [[Call]] copy and a proxy's slots
  under one borrow, and the [[Get]] and [[Set]] entries test for a proxy in the look at the kind
  they make already (mapped arguments and string wrappers; arguments objects).

As designed: ProxyData in a payload cell without a finalizer (two Values and a bool;
`needs_drop` is false, asserted); the tag after Array's, so KIND_CALLABLE_FIRST,
KIND_EXOTIC_NONE_LAST and KIND_ORDINARY_LAST stay ranges, which a proxy now fails as it already
failed `ic_plain` (still clear: the property caches stay off it); callability in the payload, as
SpiderMonkey asks the handler (V8 and JSC choose the proxy's map or structure by it); one test
per holder in the `instanceof` walk, as V8's HasInPrototypeChain makes (V8 c8b70908
src/codegen/code-stub-assembler.cc:13663-13725: each hop's map instance type, JS_PROXY_TYPE to the
runtime). Every other side table is as it was.

Where the build differs from the design:
1. The tag is 32, not the next free one: bit 5 is set in no other kind's tag (all are below 32),
   and the walk tests it with one TBNZ. A new kind takes a tag below 32, or one with the bit if its
   [[GetPrototypeOf]] is not the field read either (value.rs; jit_layout_tests::
   only_a_proxys_kind_tag_has_the_proxy_bit checks the kinds JavaScript makes).
2. JitCtx's slot [32] stays, unused, rather than moving the five fixed offsets after it, which
   every template reads by number.
3. Revocation keeps the target, as the side table did (the spec nulls it; nothing observes it):
   typeof, IsCallable and IsConstructor of a revoked proxy come from the payload and the flag
   bit, and every operation tests the handler.
4. A native parent's graft in super() (eval.rs; %Proxy% reached as the parent through a changed
   [[Prototype]]) leaves a proxy's state with it, as the side table did, rather than making the
   new `this` a proxy whose `ic_plain` is set.
5. Tests: the side-slot record tests use a promise and a class where they used a proxy, and check
   that a proxy owns no side slot (table_record_tests); the owner-index test routes a Realm's
   record (agent_control_tests); Interp's inventory has two fields fewer (149). New:
   tests::instanceof_walks_ask_a_proxy_on_the_chain_through_its_trap (three tiers: a proxy as the
   left operand, mid-chain and revoked, a warmed site with a proxy alive elsewhere) and the tag
   test above.

### W6: incremental marking (census, survey and design; the owner's questions open, 2026-11-04)

W6 as planned (Decision 4): a marking write barrier in the interpreter, the VM and both JIT
backends, and major marking in slices interleaved with the program, as V8's incremental marking
runs; concurrent marking stays a non-goal; marking's exit is set in this note, with SplayLatency at
least the old engine's (6446) as the target. Census and survey on main 8f8139f0, whose engine is
cbab4c2f's; no engine change on main. Everything below is in target/p2/w6 (untracked; README.txt
lists the files). A draft: the decisions at its end are the owner's.

What exists:
- A major collection is one pause: the engine's whole collection (gc_collect.rs:1127-1275). The
  client is built (gc_collect.rs:642-756); the heap clears every mark and card, then marks the
  roots, the native stack, the side tables and ephemerons, and drains (gc_core.rs:3283-3420); the
  engine evicts the dead from its tables and clears weak handles between the phases; the heap
  sweeps every page (gc_collect.rs:1343-1390; gc_core.rs:3518-3633).
- Collections run only at safepoints, when the poll words' heap bit says one is due: the
  allocator's byte check raises it (gc_core.rs:2171-2196), and gc_check runs the collection, from
  the VM, the tree-walker and generated code's polls (interpreter.rs:13273-13320;
  bytecode.rs:29190-29220). Allocation never collects.
- Marks are sticky, in side bitmaps (gc_core.rs:938-993): between collections a marked cell is
  old. A minor collection reads them to tell old from young; a major clears them first.
- The barrier stores the written cell's card and its page's summary, from the address alone, with
  no load and no branch (gc_core.rs:101-122). Rust calls it at every mutable borrow of an object or
  environment (gc_handle.rs:90-110, env_handle.rs:88-107) and at five other sites (closure caches,
  private property layouts, deferred prototypes twice, the VM's captured stores). Generated code
  stores the same bytes after every store of a word that can be a reference: ten ARM64 sites of
  one emitter (jit.rs:11904-11941), three x86-64 sites (jit_x64_names.rs:374-390). Rust and
  x86-64 store 1, ARM64 0xff; a set card is any nonzero byte.
- What a minor collection consumes besides the cards, each a record of writes since the last
  collection: ClientRecords (side-slot owners, WeakMap entries, native functions' realms;
  gc_collect.rs:273-337), the handles written (handles.rs:112-140), code roots and their late
  stores (value.rs:3688-3710), the shape directory's and atom table's young lists, the closure
  registry's stamp (value.rs:5304-5345), and the dirty runs of element blocks of more than 64
  words (word_block.rs:109-111).
- Black allocation exists for the window between a collection's marking and its sweep
  (gc_core.rs:2292-2303, 2398-2403). In-line allocation (W2e) takes cells unmarked.
- Pacing (W6a, gc_pacing.rs): the next budget comes from V8's bounded limit
  (gc_pacing.rs:111-121) with a growing factor from the major's speed, its marked bytes over its
  pause (gc_pacing.rs:314-364).

Census (target/p2/w6: scripts/, runs/, counts/, splay/, and census-tables.md and
census-tables-s1.md, which hold every table of the two sessions in full; commit 4a4d8b40 on branch
p2-w6-census, from main 8f8139f0; fat LTO,
target/p2/lto/8f8139f0 (main) and target/p2/w6/lto-census (the census build)):
- Method. Main's engine ran each workload with TRUST_JS_GC_LOG=1 at the default pacing (the
  fixtures at --tier=jit, the sustained workload, chai, the Octane benchmarks at the fixed driver's
  5 runs with clock.js, and Octane's own driver over splay.js, "splay-real", which scores
  SplayLatency). The census build (scripts/apply-census.py) adds: a counter at each barrier site
  (Rust's nine callers, ARM64's ten emitter sites; x86-64 is not counted on Crystal); the card byte
  read as bits, every barrier storing 0xff, a minor collection clearing bit 0 alone (as it clears
  the byte now), bit 1 kept from one major to the next, and bits 2-5 cleared by samples taken at the
  first safepoint after every 64 KB of allocation and every 4th, 16th and 64th (64 KB, 256 KB, 1 MB
  and 4 MB windows: a slice's preclean, simulated); each sample counts the set cards, the marked
  (old) and unmarked (young) cells that start in them, and traces each old one with its full trace,
  testing every edge against the marks (the rescan, as a proxy); the GC log's majors add their
  marked bytes and conditional edges, and a first drain from the roots and stack alone before the
  side tables. Counts: main's instructions on CPUs 10-13 (setarch -R, pacing off, one run each,
  scripts/counts.sh); barrier counts with the census build at pacing off.
- Load. The machine never fell under the plan's quiet threshold (2 cores): another session's
  Test262 under GC stress, its builds and counts, and a game. The first runs (runs/gclog-main,
  cards-64k, barriers-off) had 9-19 other cores busy; a second session at 15:44
  (scripts/session-now.sh, the quiet session's script without its gate) had 2.5-7.6, its Splay runs
  3.0-5.1 (median 3.8). Every run's other load is in its summary.jsonl. Counts, cards, cells and
  edges do not depend on the load (each window is a number of bytes allocated); times do. The
  tables take the second session's runs where it made them (runs/gclog-s2, cards-s2,
  splaylat-main-r1..r10) and say so where they do not; the two sessions' pauses agree within 10%.

Majors at the default pacing (main, CPU 15; the largest of each workload; ms; Gameboy from the first

Minor collections (main, the same runs; pause ms; promoted MB; the minor drain's MB per ms):

- A major's pause is its drain: 84-99% where the heap is large (Splay, TypeScript, the sustained
  workload, EarleyBoyer), 23-59% where it is small and the roots and side tables weigh more
  (chai 2.4 MB, Gameboy, PdfJS). The drain marks 1.6-3.0 MB a ms (1.8-1.9 on the two largest
  heaps).
- What is left of a major once marking leaves its pause: the roots and stack, 0.1-1.8 ms; the side
  tables, 0.1-3.2 ms (Gameboy's 17,023 conditional edges); the engine's steps, 0.1-1.8 ms; the core
  sweep, 0.0-1.6 ms. Splay's two last majors also spend 7.3 and 6.9 ms in their sweep outside every
  timed step, user time absent from a perf profile of the run (target/p2/w6/perf): the kernel's,
  most likely the per-page discard of the spare pages beyond the cap (gc_core.rs:4264-4278), each
  a separate call [inferred; perf at paranoid 2 samples no kernel time].
- Every major runs at the safepoint after the minor whose sweep made it due, so the pause the
  program sees is both: Splay's are 17-18 ms of minor and 58-69 ms of major.
- Splay's minor collections take 17.5 ms each: its nursery grows to 32 MB (V8's largest
  semi-space; the survivors pass the budget) and nearly all of it survives, so each minor promotes
  31.9 MB at 1.9 MB a ms. TypeScript's take 13.5-44 ms, at half the rate: its card cells,
  29,663-214,969 a minor, are W2f's card pass.

SplayLatency (Octane's own driver over splay.js; main; score = 100 x 2,739,514 / RMS, the RMS in
units of 0.1 us of Date.now's 1 ms clock, this shell having no performance.now):
- Today: 5,645, the median of 10 runs (5,290-5,765; Splay 4,515) on CPU 15 with 3.0-5.1 other cores
  busy; 4,365-5,535 in the first session's three runs under 10-17. The close-out measured 3,845, the
  old engine 6,446.
- The diagnostic (splay/stats.js and report.js wrap SplayUpdateStats and change nothing it
  computes; three runs, splay/diag-r1..r3.txt) reproduces the score: 1,465-1,496 samples whose
  squared pauses sum to 34,861-37,117 ms^2, of which 45-46 samples of 3 ms or more carry
  33,495-35,764: the collections. The rest, about 1 ms each (Date.now's resolution), sum to about
  1,390. The four largest samples, 84-86, 83-85, 74-77 and 41-42 ms, are each a minor and the major
  it made due; they alone carry 22,145 ms^2 of run 2's 35,774.
- 6,446 needs the squared pauses to average at most 18.1 ms^2 a sample, about 27,000 over 1,495
  [arithmetic]. With the majors' part of those four samples removed, the sum falls to about 14,700
  (9.8 a sample: about 8,700) [arithmetic]. Spreading each large cycle's marking over its samples
  (design 4) adds about 1,200; the four 18 ms minors each of the three large cycles suspends
  (design 2) take about 3,900 away: about 12,000, about 9,700 [arithmetic]. The ceiling, with all
  of Splay's collection spread evenly, is the 1.46 ms average sample: about 18,700 [arithmetic].

- So a flag test's lower bound is 0.00-0.33% of instructions. Its Rust form cannot be a value
  barrier where it stands: the borrow comes before the stores and does not see them. The object
  model writes through 895 `.borrow_mut()` calls in 71 files (every RefCell's, so an upper bound on
  the objects' and environments').

- The cards' rescan is small where writes repeat: Splay's whole interval, 216 ms of program and
  235 MB allocated, leaves 33,404 cards and 1.1 ms. Its hot cells (the nodes near the tree's root)
  are written in every window, so precleaning each window rescans them each time: 46-93 us a ms of
  program, the most of any workload but the sustained one.
- It is large where writes spread: TypeScript writes 417-428 distinct cards a ms of program at
  both window sizes, and its interval since the last major leaves 670,000 to 1.1 million cards,
  84-131 MB of old cells and 56-109 ms of rescan. Per 64 KB window the rescan is 6 us at the
  median, 101 us at p95 and 7.6 ms in its largest burst; precleaning costs it 23-31 us a ms of
  program.
- A large element block makes one old cell expensive: the sustained workload rewrites an array of
  200,025 words, whose owner's rescan traces every word, up to 1.5 ms a window (1,550 us a ms).
  A minor collection reads such a block's dirty runs; a major rescan has none.
- The side tables reach little (census build's first drain, before them): 0-2.8% of the marked
  bytes, but Gameboy's 16.7% (0.7 MB through 17,023 conditional edges; 3.0 ms of side tables and
  0.8 ms of drain).

What the exemplars do (target/p2/w6/exemplars.txt, A1-A14; the per-engine reports
exemplars-v8.txt, exemplars-sm.txt and exemplars-jsc.txt; V8 c8b70908, SM 6bb81100, JSC 26027804,
each checked at its main of 2026-11-04, where the cited code holds but for one V8 range noted there;
V8's report 340 ranges, SM's 338, JSC's 354, the summary's 111, 0 problems):
- A1: V8's barrier shades the stored value (Dijkstra), SM's the overwritten one (snapshot at the
  beginning), JSC's the holder: a black holder stored into turns grey and is queued for a rescan,
  in the same stack that is its remembered set between collections. V8 and SM get the value at
  every store from their field types; JSC barriers the holder after the store, as TRust before it.
- A2: with marking off a barrier costs V8 4-10 instructions on ARM64, SM 5-8, JSC 7.
- A3: V8's young objects and all of JSC's are allocated white; SM's tenured cells black.
- A4: V8 runs no scavenge while it marks ("Incremental marking forced finalization"; the young
  generation grows instead until a large overshoot), and JSC no Eden collection inside a Full one;
  SM collects the nursery before marking its roots and lets minors run between slices, safe
  because its snapshot keeps every promoted cell's referents.
- A5: V8 starts at a soft limit, when the headroom below its limit falls to one young generation's
  capacity, and marks the roots without the stack; SM at a zone's start threshold, with an
  incremental limit of 1.7x down to 1.1x it ("at least 1.7 to maintain performance on
  splay-latency").
- A6: V8's steps come every 64 KB of young and 256 KB of old allocation and from tasks, 5 ms and
  1 ms at most, toward a 500 ms cycle; with concurrent marking off each step asks 64 KB. SM slices
  at 1 MiB of allocation past the last slice, 5 ms in the shell. JSC's mutator marks in proportion
  to its allocation only on one core.
- A7: V8 marks every root at the start and again at the final pause; SM once, at the start
  (the snapshot needs no rescan); JSC reruns its root constraints whenever the program has run.
- A8: V8's final pause re-marks the roots, closes with the ephemeron fixpoint, scans the stack and
  clears weak references; it finalizes once the worklists are empty, and is forced past an
  overshoot margin of min(max(limit / 2, 32 MB), (maximum - limit) / 2).
- A9: ephemerons are resolved at the end in V8 (discovered in steps) and JSC (a fixpoint
  constraint); SM marks weak maps incrementally through a table of key edges.
- A10: V8 grows its heap with the combined speed of the incremental steps and the final pause; its
  memory reducer starts incremental marking.
- A11: SM's gray marking serves the embedding's cycle collector; TRust has none.
- A12: each engine's generated code shares one slow path (V8's RecordWrite builtin, SM's
  trampolines, JSC's operationWriteBarrierSlowPath) and reads its flag from an address it embeds.
- A13: JSC's fences, its tautological threshold and its race stack exist for concurrency alone.
- A14: all three sweep outside the pause (concurrently, in slices, or on allocation).

Design:
1. The barrier is the card barrier as it stands: no new instruction at any site.
   - During a cycle a set card names cells written since the cycle began or since the last
     preclean. A marked cell on a set card may hold an edge the marker has not seen, and the marker
     rescans it: JSC's re-grey of the holder (A1), at a card's granularity, which Boehm, Demers and
     Shenker's mostly-parallel collector also used. Rust, the VM and both backends already store
     the bytes it reads.
   - A value barrier (V8's or SM's, A1) needs the stored or the overwritten value at each store. The
     Rust barrier sits at the borrow, before the stores (A1: JSC's place), and the object model has
     no field type that every store goes through, as V8's and SM's have: 895 `.borrow_mut()` calls
     write through it. A store a value barrier missed would free a live cell.
   - Its price would be at least a load and a branch at every barrier, 0.00-0.33% of instructions,
     and 0.00-1.65% at A2's 4-10 instructions a barrier [arithmetic]. The cards cost no instruction
     at a store; they cost the rescans (design 5 and the final pause).
   - The cycle's start clears every card (as a major's start does now) and the final pause clears
     them again, so the next minor collection finds only the writes made after it.
   - A second bit a card (a minor bit and a major bit in the byte every barrier stores, so no new
     instruction) is what minor collections during a cycle would need: the census build is that
     scheme (bit 0 the minors', bit 1 the cycle's), and its tables are the rescans' cost. With no
     minor collection in a cycle (design 2) the one bit suffices.
2. No minor collection while a cycle marks (V8's and JSC's rule, A4).
   - A minor collection that falls due during a cycle is not run: the nursery's budget is suspended
     and the young generation grows, as V8's does, until the cycle ends.
   - So the marks keep one meaning, this cycle's; a minor collection needs no change; the card byte
     needs no second bit. The marker marks young cells as it reaches them, and the final pause,
     a major collection's end, sweeps every page and leaves every live cell old.
   - The price: the young garbage allocated during the cycle waits for its final pause, at most
     the allowance (264-302 MB on Splay and TypeScript, 67 MB on the smaller heaps).
   - SM's alternative (A4) would need its snapshot invariant: with a holder barrier a promoted cell
     must be grey or rescanned, and minors would need their age apart from the cycle's marks, a
     second bitmap a page. Not taken.
3. Cells allocated during a cycle are white (V8's young space, JSC; A3).
   - Allocation and in-line allocation do not change. An initializing store before the next
     safepoint needs no barrier, as now, since a slice runs only at a safepoint. The prologue's
     copies into an in-line record, which set no card (jit.rs:12519-12555), stay safe for the same
     reason.
   - The final pause's window between its marking and its sweep keeps today's black allocation.
   - Not black during the cycle (SM's tenured cells, V8's old space): a black cell is not traced,
     and a new cell's initializing stores (in-line allocation's template copy, Rust's construction
     through Gc::object_ptr) set no card, so a black new cell holding the only edge to a white cell
     would lose it. SM's snapshot keeps that cell's referent marked; a holder barrier does not
     [inferred]. White allocation's price is the marking of the cycle's survivors, which a minor
     collection would otherwise do (Splay's case).
4. Slices.
   - Due once 64 KB more were allocated since the last slice (V8's young step, A6), through the heap
     bit's byte check as a collection is due now (gc_core.rs:2435-2445), at the next safepoint;
     gc_check runs it. Deferred as a collection is, in no-GC regions and under borrows.
   - Its work: the marked bytes the schedule asks, the larger of V8's time schedule (500 ms a
     cycle) and an allocation schedule that ends marking by half the allowance, counting the
     slices' own bytes (V8's main thread counts none, A6); capped at 1 ms (V8's task step; it
     allows 5 ms on allocation, SM's shell 5 ms). At 1.8 MB a ms a slice marks about 1.8 MB.
   - Between slices the program runs, with no minor collection (design 2).
5. Precleaning.
   - When the worklist empties, a slice scans the page summaries and rescans the marked cells on set
     cards, clears those cards and drains what the rescan reaches (JSC rescans its re-grey queue at
     every stop, A1, A7).
   - Only after the worklist empties, not on a timer: Splay's hot cells would be rescanned at every
     preclean (46-93 us a ms of program), while its whole cycle leaves 1.1 ms.
   - Repeated until a preclean finds less than the final pause's budget for it (0.5 ms of rescan:
     about 7,000 old cells at the 67-78 ns a cell of TypeScript's whole-interval rescans)
     [arithmetic; to be set by measurement].
6. Start and finalization (V8's rules, A5, A8).
   - Start: at the safepoint after the minor collection whose sweep leaves the heap within one
     nursery budget of the byte budget (V8's soft limit, A5); today that collection would make a
     major due at the budget (gc_core.rs:3578). The first slice clears the marks and cards (the
     begin phase, 0.4-0.6 ms on the largest heaps), reports the roots and the native stack (0.1-1.8
     ms) and drains within its budget. Consuming the minor collections' records there is harmless:
     no minor runs before the final pause, which reports everything.
   - No cycle while the heap holds 8 MB or less: such a major stays one pause, about 4 ms at most
     at the census's marking rate (V8's activation threshold, 8 MB in release builds and 0 in debug
     builds, V8 src/heap/incremental-marking.cc:62-68, 135-138; TRust's budget floor is also 8 MB,
     gc_collect.rs:50).
   - Finalize at the first safepoint after a preclean found the dirty set below its budget and the
     worklist empty.
   - Forced: when the cycle's allocation passes V8's overshoot margin over the budget (A8), the next
     safepoint finishes the marking in one pause, the old major's failure mode. Also at once for
     the requests that want a collection now: explicit ones ($262.gc, a host's, the exit and idle
     collections), the live-object ceiling and ArrayBuffer pressure.
7. The final pause.
   - A major collection's marking with the cycle's marks kept: the client (Marking::new), the
     roots, the native stack, the strong handles and the code roots, all as a major reports them;
     the marked cells on the cards still set; the side tables and the ephemerons in full; the drain;
     then today's engine steps and sweep. Every root again, as V8's pause (A7, A8): TRust has no
     barrier on roots.
   - Its cost from the census (the final-pause table): roots and stack 0.1-1.8 ms, side tables
     0.1-3.2 ms, the cards left by the last preclean (design 5) and the drain of what they reach,
     the engine's steps 0.1-1.8 ms, the core sweep 0.0-1.6 ms: 0.4-5.1 ms on every workload measured
     [arithmetic]. Splay's late majors add their 6.9-7.3 ms of untimed sweep work, which moves out
     of the pause (order, step 5).
8. Weak processing, ephemerons and finalization at the final pause, as now (V8's resolution and
   JSC's fixpoint, A8, A9). The side tables reach 0-2.8% of the marked bytes on every workload but
   Gameboy (16.7%, 3.0 ms). V8's discovery in steps or SM's edge table is a later step, if a
   workload needs it.
9. Pacing and the memory reducer.
   - A major's speed for the growing factor: its marked bytes over the cycle's whole marking time,
     slices and final pause (V8's combined speed, A10). Over the final pause alone the speed would
     be tens of times the drain's, and the factor would fall toward its minimum, 1.1 [inferred from
     gc_pacing.rs:65-84].
   - The budget's rule (W6a) is unchanged; the cycle's allocation runs above it, within the margin.
   - The memory reducer's collection stays one pause: it runs when the program allocates slowly.
     V8 starts incremental marking for it (A10): owner's decision.
10. The JIT changes nothing in either backend: the barrier stays (design 1), in-line allocation
    stays white (design 3), slices enter through the existing poll (jit_interrupt), and no address
    of a heap enters generated code, so the process-wide shared stubs are untouched.
11. Verification.
    - TRUST_JS_GC_VERIFY extends the write barrier's check (gc_core.rs:3468-3516) to the cycle: at
      every slice's end and at the final pause, a marked cell whose card is clean holds no edge to
      an allocated unmarked cell. It catches a missed barrier where it matters; the final pause's
      verify (gc_core.rs:3848-3906) runs as now.
    - TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=force makes every major a cycle with slices of a few cells at every
      safepoint; with GC stress, the lib suite and Test262 run under it and the verification (the
      memory note's lesson: Test262 under stress finds unrooted values the gates miss).

Order (each step measured on its own):
1. The log: slices and final pauses in TRUST_JS_GC_LOG, the cycle's allocation and marking time.
2. The cycle behind TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL (off by default): the marker's worklist kept across
   slices; the start, the slices and the final pause; minors suspended; finalization when the
   worklist empties; the forced finalization; verification (design 11). No dump changes.
3. Precleaning and its finalization rule (design 5).
4. The schedule: the start rule, the budgets, the 1 ms cap; pacing's combined speed (design 9).
5. The spare pages' release out of the final pause (trim_spare_pages, gc_core.rs:4264-4278): at the
   next slices, or batched, as V8's unmapper and SM's decommit work outside the pause (A14).
6. Measurement, then on by default: the exit's timing on a quiet machine.
7. Later, each measured first: a major rescan's own dirty runs for large element blocks and
   payloads; ephemerons in steps; the memory reducer's collection as a cycle; idle slices from the
   runtime's event loop (V8's tasks, A6).

Change surface:
- gc_core.rs: the Heap's cycle (its worklist and phase, its budgets and allocation since the start);
  mark_phase and begin_marking split into the cycle's start, its slices and the final marking
  (gc_core.rs:3283-3420); drain under a budget (gc_core.rs:3727-3775); the due logic
  (collection_due, bytes_due, due_kind, refresh_due; gc_core.rs:2020-2057, 2171-2196) with slices
  and the suspended nursery; sweep_phase's pacing call with the cycle's marking time
  (gc_core.rs:3518-3633); the write barrier's check (gc_core.rs:3468-3516); trim_spare_pages
  (gc_core.rs:4264-4278).
- gc_collect.rs: gc_heap_collect_active dispatches a cycle's start, a slice or its final pause
  (gc_collect.rs:1127-1275); gc_heap_mark splits; the client is built at the start and at the final
  pause only (gc_collect.rs:642-756).
- value.rs: mark_agent_heap and the closure registry's stamp kept across a cycle's slices
  (value.rs:5304-5345).
- gc_pacing.rs: Pacing::start and end with the cycle's marking time (gc_pacing.rs:302-364).
- interpreter.rs: gc_check's dispatch (interpreter.rs:13273-13320), and the task boundary's
  optional collection, which becomes a slice during a cycle (interpreter.rs:13324-13352).
- Unchanged: gc_handle.rs, env_handle.rs, jit.rs, jit_operations.rs, jit_x64_names.rs, jit_alloc.rs.
- Tests: a cycle's slices and final pause keep every reachable cell (all tiers, ShadowRealms
  sharing a heap, a host graph); a store into a marked cell between slices, through every barrier
  site (Rust's nine, ARM64's ten, x86-64's three), is rescanned; the forced finalization at the
  margin; an explicit collection during a cycle; no minor collection during a cycle; the cards clean
  after the final pause; pacing's speed over a cycle.

Risks:
- A missed barrier is a use-after-free, now for any edge stored into a marked cell, old or young.
  Today only an old cell's edge to a young cell matters, and the write barrier's check verifies it.
  Every write path's card_mark is the barrier; the raw writes (Gc::object_ptr, Env::scope_ptr) are
  initializing stores into fresh cells before any safepoint (value.rs:2985-3035;
  interpreter.rs:2440-2460). Design 11 is the mitigation, run at the stage's end.
- Memory: the cycle's young garbage (design 2) raises peak RSS where a large heap is marked while
  the program allocates fast. The margin bounds it.
- The marking moves, it does not shrink: Splay's slices take about half of each cycle. Precleaning
  adds rescans of what was written, most where writes spread (TypeScript, 23-31 us a ms of program
  while it runs).
- A burst of writes just before the final pause enlarges it (TypeScript's largest 64 KB window: 7.6
  ms of rescan), and so does a forced finalization.
- The schedule's numbers (64 KB, 1 ms, the finalization budget) are V8's or guesses until
  measured.

Exit (proposed):
- SplayLatency >= 6446 (the plan's), median of 10 on a quiet machine (5,645 today with 3.0-5.1
  other cores busy). Estimated about 8,700 with the majors' pauses removed and the minors
  unchanged, about 9,700 when each of the three large cycles also suspends the four 32 MB minors it
  spans and spreads its 126 ms of marking over its samples (design 2), and at most about 18,700
  with all of Splay's collection spread evenly [arithmetic, from the census's samples].
- No pause of a major collection, a slice or a final pause, above 5 ms on the fixtures, chai, the
  sustained workload and Octane at the default pacing, where the largest today are 276 ms
  (TypeScript) and 69 ms (Splay); slices at most 1 ms but for the one that starts a cycle. The
  estimates leave chai and Gameboy little room (4.3-4.9 ms: their roots, side tables and table
  sweeps). Minor collections are not W6's: Splay's take 17.5 ms and TypeScript's up to 44 ms.
- No workload slower beyond noise in instructions at pacing off, but for precleaning where a
  workload marks during most of its run, held to 1% [to be confirmed by the implementation's own
  numbers].
- Test262 identical; the lib suite and Test262 under GC stress with TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=force
  and TRUST_JS_GC_VERIFY.
- Peak RSS reported beside it (fixtures, Octane, Web Tooling), not bounded.

Recommended (mine): each as the design above has it (the census's and the agent's survey's
answers: the cards because a value barrier cannot be complete in Rust, whose barrier fires at the
borrow; V8's and JSC's order of minors and marking; white allocation, which the cards keep
correct). W6 is the plan's last stage, so nothing waits on these yet.

Decisions (the owner's):
1. The barrier: the cards as the marking barrier, with no instruction added at any site (design 1),
   where the plan's text names a new barrier in the interpreter, the VM and both backends. The
   alternative is a value barrier at every Rust store under a borrow (895 calls).
2. No minor collections while marking, as V8 and JSC (design 2), against SM's minors between
   slices and their second bitmap.
3. White allocation during a cycle (design 3).
4. Slices: V8's 64 KB step; a 1 ms cap or V8's 5 ms; the schedule (design 4).
5. Precleaning only once the worklist empties, and its finalization budget (design 5).
6. Ephemerons and weak processing at the final pause in the first version (design 8).
7. The memory reducer's and explicit collections as one pause (designs 6, 9).
8. The spare pages' release out of the pause as part of W6 (order, step 5).
9. The exit's numbers.

### The owner's answers: W6, the threshold, compact templates (2026-11-04)

The owner, about 16:50: "Your design questions are approved as recommended as long as they
aren't simply to make implementation simpler." On timing: "You can do a timing run any time that
your subagents aren't doing a build, we have 20 cores, 10 of them are fast cores, you don't have
to wait for a 2-core minimum." The timing rule replaces the 2-core trigger: a session starts when
no agent of this work builds or runs a suite, and agents hold new builds while it runs.

Each recommendation, checked against the condition:

W6 ("W6: incremental marking" above):
1. The cards as the marking barrier: as recommended. Its reasons are soundness and cost: a value
   barrier needs the stored or overwritten value at every store, the Rust barrier fires at the
   borrow before the stores (JSC's place, A1), and a store such a barrier missed would free a live
   cell; the cards add no instruction at a store.
2. No minor collection while a cycle marks: as recommended. Current V8 (a young-generation request
   during marking selects the mark-compactor and the scavenger asserts that marking is off, A4)
   and JSC (one request a cycle) both; TRust's minors mark in place with the major's bits, as JSC's
   Eden collections do, where SM's minors between slices copy out of a nursery. It also lifts
   SplayLatency (about 9,700 against 8,700 with the minors kept, the exit's estimates). Its price,
   the cycle's young garbage, is bounded by V8's margin.
3. White allocation during a cycle: as recommended (V8's young space and all of JSC's): no store
   at an allocation; its price is the marking of the cycle's survivors.
4. Slices every 64 KB, capped at 1 ms: as recommended (V8's young step and task budget). The cap
   is the exit's latency, to be set by measurement.
5. Precleaning once the worklist empties: as recommended, a cost choice (Splay's hot cells would
   be rescanned at every timed preclean).
6. Changed to V8's: ephemerons are discovered in the slices and resolved at the final pause. The
   draft left all of it to the pause in a first version because it is small, an argument from
   ease. As V8 (src/heap/marking-visitor-inl.h:696-806; src/heap/mark-compact.cc:2142-2198,
   2249-2285): a slice that traces a weak collection marks the values of its marked keys and
   records the unresolved pairs; a weak reference or finalization cell whose target is unmarked
   goes onto the cycle's weak list; the final pause merges the recorded pairs with the weak
   collections on set cards, runs the fixpoint (V8's ten rounds, then its linear algorithm), and
   clears and queues after marking, as now. The side-slot tables, which V8 has no counterpart of,
   go the same way: their conditional edges are traced in the slices as their owners are marked,
   as a major traces them now, and the final pause takes only the owners written during the cycle
   (ClientRecords' set, the tables' cards) rather than every table in full (Gameboy's 3.0 ms of
   side tables in the census's pause). It follows W2g step 5, whose WeakMap representation the
   trace reads.
7. Changed to V8's for the memory reducer: its collection starts a cycle (V8
   src/heap/memory-reducer.cc:92-105, incremental marking with kReduceMemoryFootprint). The draft
   kept one pause because the program then allocates slowly, so allocation would not bring the
   slices; V8 runs them from tasks (IncrementalMarkingJob, A6), and so will TRust: the engine
   reports the cycle's next slice deadline beside memory_reducer_deadline, and trust-js-runtime's
   loop runs a slice when it is due, as it runs the reducer's timer
   (crates/trust-js-runtime/src/lib.rs:510-513). Explicit collections ($262.gc, a host's, the
   exit's), the live-object ceiling and ArrayBuffer pressure finish a running cycle at once in
   one pause, as V8's full collections do: as recommended.
8. The spare pages' release out of the pause, in W6: as recommended.
9. The exit's numbers: as proposed.
So the order's step 7 loses three items to W6 itself: ephemerons and the side tables in the
slices (after step 2, before precleaning), and the reducer's cycle with the event loop's slices
(with the schedule, step 4). A large block's own dirty runs stay measured first: JSC re-greys the
whole holder too, and the census does not say whether TypeScript's 7.6 ms burst is large cells'.

The threshold: as recommended, the exemplars' compile at the first call with TRust's pages reusing
their compiled platform code (the phase exit's candidates), now that the timing can run; the
timing on today's main decides it against the counts' mixed signs (record above).

Compact baseline templates: as recommended. The exemplars' baselines call shared IC stubs or
builtins (V8's Sparkplug, SM's Baseline with CacheIR stubs, JSC's Baseline with shared thunks),
and TRust already shares stubs for name reads, property probes and calls outside hot code
(use_shared_stub). The sites outside hot code that still emit hundreds of bytes take that
mechanism (StrictEq, SetProp, the first property and call probe of a site first); hot code keeps
today's in-line templates. A design note first, with the census of template bytes by operation.

### W2g step 5: WeakMap's and WeakSet's data in the object (record, 2026-11-04)

Commits, from main 50c474de, on p2-w2g-rest (an agent's; worktree target/p2/w2g-rest-wt), landed
on main as 65bf3bfc (58cbbfbe) and fd0ddfe8 (82ef8fab), whose code is the measured commits' (main's
commits since 50c474de change only this plan; the measurements below name the branch's SHAs):
- 58cbbfbe: room in the ordinary kinds' tag range for the payload kinds of steps 2, 4 and 5.
  WeakMaps and WeakSets, ArrayBuffers, DataViews and RegExps have ordinary internal methods, so
  their kinds must stay inside KIND_ORDINARY_LAST, or every property cache's ordinary-object
  guard (one unsigned compare) would turn their receivers away. Tags 16 to 19, after
  Collection's (15, now KIND_COLLECTION_TAG), are theirs: KIND_ORDINARY_LAST is 19, and Array
  and the kinds after it move up by four (Array 20, still KIND_ORDINARY_LAST + 1 for the
  "ordinary or Array" guard; the wrappers 21 to 25, Error 26, Arguments 27, the iterators 28 to
  30), all below the Proxy tag's bit 5. kinds_ok and the layout tests check the new values.
- 82ef8fab: a WeakMap's and WeakSet's data in its object. ObjectKind::WeakCollection(PayloadBox<
  weak_metadata::WeakCollection>) (tag 16) holds the collection's kind and one map of its
  entries by key identity (WeakKey -> (WeakTarget, value)): the brand is the object's kind, a
  get or has one probe of the payload's map, under one borrow (nf_weak_map_get). A write goes
  through the object's mutable borrow, which sets its card, and records its entry for the next
  minor collection (ClientRecords::record_weak_entry, from WeakCollection::put), as the side
  table's writes did; a new key subscribes the collection to its target's death, as before. The
  payload cell's finalizer drops the map. Interp's weak_collection_data and
  weak_collection_index go; in their place a registry of the interpreter's collections by
  address (weak_collections, a FastSet), which only the collector reads: a major collection
  registers each registered collection's entries as ephemerons, a minor one finds a recorded
  entry's collection there, and gc_forget_weak_owners drops a dead collection's subscriptions
  and registration before its sweep (the smaller of the registry and the dead set iterated, as
  before). super()'s graft moves the kind with the other payload kinds; the registration, the
  subscriptions and the records follow it (move_weak_slots). The memory inventory counts the
  payload in the object visitor and the registry in the side tables.

As designed (A6: V8's `table`, SpiderMonkey's WeakMap in a slot, JSC's WeakMapImpl in the cell):
the brand probe and the data probe go and a get is one probe of the collection's own map; the
ephemeron records stay per entry.

Where the build differs from the design:
1. A registry stays, a set of addresses with no data: the GC core takes ephemerons only from
   the client's callback (MarkClient::ephemerons), which must enumerate the live collections at
   a major collection, and a dead collection's subscriptions in weak_metadata's target index
   must go before its cell is swept. The mutator touches it only when a collection is made.
   A minor collection's recorded entry is looked up only if its owner is registered, so a
   record that outlived its collection (or another interpreter's) never names a freed cell.
2. The pin stays. The registration and the subscriptions are the interpreter's metadata, which
   a ShadowRealm's interpreter must keep while one of its collections lives elsewhere
   (agent_control_tests::agent_kept_prototype_null_native_owners_preserve_metadata_and_then_
   retire failed without it: the child interpreter retired while its WeakMap was alive).
3. The kinds take tags 16 to 19 inside the ordinary range (58cbbfbe) rather than following
   Array's (the design's note): after Array they would fail the property caches' guard.
4. Interp's inventory has one field fewer (148).

### The tier threshold, timed (record, 2026-11-04)

For the owner's threshold decision ("The owner's answers" above: the timing decides it). Main's
engine a31509fe (fat LTO, target/p2/lto/a31509fe; main f3d0622e's engine adds only W2g step 5),
pinned to CPU 5 (an X925 core), rounds rotating the engines, the fixtures' own elapsed_ms
(medians), at moments when no agent built (the hold, target/p2/timing/HOLD; the other load
0.5-3.7 cores, mostly two single-threaded Test262 stress workers). Everything is in
target/p2/threshold-t1 (session.sh, session2.sh, session3.sh, counts-env.sh and their outputs).

How a function tiers today: its first 8 calls (TRUST_JS_TIER_THRESHOLD) run in the tree-walker,
which fills no cache; then it compiles to bytecode, and a function without loops compiles to
native code at its first bytecode run (TRUST_JS_JIT_ADMIT_RUNS, default 0), so its first native
code is made with every cache empty. The exemplars compile to bytecode at the first call and to
baseline code once the interpreter has run it and filled its feedback (V8's Sparkplug after a
budget of Ignition, JSC's Baseline after LLInt, SpiderMonkey's Baseline after the Baseline
Interpreter).

Session 1 (10 rounds of the fixtures with Node limited to Sparkplug, 3 of Octane, 1 of Web
Tooling): threshold 1 (t1) against 8 (t8).

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Djot | 93 ms | 83 (-10.8%) | 38 | 2.45x | 2.18x |
| React | 31 | 33 (+6.5%) | 16 | 1.94x | 2.06x |
| Vue | 260 | 262 (+0.8%) | 113 | 2.30x | 2.32x |

peak RSS -16.6%: another collection schedule), Gameboy +1.4%. Web Tooling (runs a second, higher

-3.3%, babel-minify -2.4%, source-map -1.8%. Threshold 1 compiles to native code at a function's second call,
before any cache has a state: React pays for the compiles of functions it calls a few times.

Decision: the threshold stays at 8 for now. Every variant that compiles earlier costs TRust's
event-loop page 76-130% of its engine time, which is the condition the recommendation named
(TRust's pages reusing their compiled platform code); and at t8 too every page compiles 1.18 MB of
machine code for the same platform functions. So the reuse comes first, as its own design note
(the exemplars: V8's code cache and its isolate-independent embedded builtins, SpiderMonkey's
shared script data, JSC's bytecode cache), with the compact templates (which shrink every compile
at any threshold); then the threshold, where t1a2 is the measured choice (Djot -9.5%, React -3.2%,
Vue 0.0% on the fixtures' timers).

### Compact baseline templates (census, survey and design, 2026-11-04)

The owner approved compact baseline templates on 2026-11-04 ("The owner's answers" above): the
sites outside hot code that still emit hundreds of bytes take the shared-stub mechanism, hot code
keeps today's in-line templates; a design note first. Census on main a31509fe's engine (fat LTO,
target/p2/lto/a31509fe; main f3ab7b2b's engine adds W2g step 5); tools and data in target/p2/compact (untracked): opbytes.py (bytes by
operation from a TRUST_JS_JIT_MAP=1 log), opsamples.py (the same split by instruction samples),
census.sh.

What exists:
- Tiering. A function runs its first 8 calls (TRUST_JS_TIER_THRESHOLD; backedges count 1/16) in
  the tree-walker, which fills no cache (W4's census). Its first native compile happens at its
  first bytecode run (TRUST_JS_JIT_ADMIT_RUNS, default 0, interpreter.rs:14884-14897), so every
  property, call and name cache of the chunk is empty when its code is made. The second stage
  (try_inline_recompile, interpreter.rs:15896-15905) recompiles a function at 100 machine-code
  runs with its callees spliced in, seeded with the warm caches (Chunk::jit_cache_preferred,
  bytecode.rs:21854-21863), and bumps the global call-cache epoch; a function with nothing to
  inline ("empty plan") keeps its first-stage code.
- So a first-stage property read bakes no probe: it probes the cache's ways through the shared
  PropWays stub (jit.rs:7234-7261), and its in-line code is the receiver's test, the stub call,
  the landings (entry and bounds, the accessor test, the `prototype` guard, the key-checked arm,
  the absent value), the commit and the slow path (jit.rs:6942-7368).
- Shared stubs: one process-wide copy each, reached through a two-instruction-target veneer per
  chunk (emit_shared_stubs, jit.rs:13810-13830). use_shared_stub (jit.rs:13730-13743) puts the
  name reads' cache proof, the direct call and construct sequences and the call intrinsics in a
  stub outside loops (`hot` = the pc is in a loop, jit.rs:5122); the property way loop, the
  secondary call probes and every slow path's helper call (three instructions a site,
  jit.rs:19455-19472) are shared everywhere.

Census (main a31509fe's engine; a site's span runs from its [jit-map-pc] offset to the next;
spans holding a `region:` mark are region code; SPE samples about one operation in 1,024, user
mode, on CPU 13 (census.sh); a site never sampled ran fewer than about a thousand operations of its
template after its compile). PMU sampling returned IP 0 for 75% of its samples here; SPE did not.

| fixture | compiles | template bytes | never sampled | region bytes | never sampled | samples in generated code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
