### TRust's pages reusing their compiled code (census, survey and scope, 2026-11-05)

The threshold's prerequisite (the threshold record above) and, as measured here, the largest
part of a small page's engine time. TRust 78435d0 on engine f3d0622e (target/p2/threshold-t1/
trust-main), the offline replays on the X925 cores, TRUST_JS_PERF_METRICS's dump per page (each
dump cumulative; a page's share is the difference; target/p2/page-reuse):

| page | engine time a page | bytecode compiles | their time | native compiles | their time | machine code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| event-loop | 28-30 ms (21 ms without metrics) | 134 | 4.5-4.7 ms | 105 | 14.5-15.0 ms | 1.23 MB |
| dom-reconcile | 1,759-1,791 ms | 246 | 7.7 ms | 215 | 28.4-29.0 ms | 2.54 MB |
| Vue TodoMVC | 533-557 ms | 693 | 22.6-24.4 ms | 655 | 104-108 ms | 9.78 MB |

Every page compiles the same functions again: the platform's (the static snapshot's prelude:
WebIDL glue such as enumerableMembers and idlImplements, the event loop's) and, on TodoMVC, the
page's own bundle (Vue's chunk-vendors.js and app.js), which every load of the page brings
unchanged. Compiling is about two thirds of the event-loop page's engine time and about a quarter
of TodoMVC's, at threshold 8; at threshold 1 with two bytecode runs the event-loop page compiles
3.4 MB.

What the exemplars do:
- JSC shares a function's baseline machine code among its CodeBlocks: the code belongs to the
  UnlinkedCodeBlock (UnlinkedCodeBlock::m_unlinkedBaselineCode,
  Source/JavaScriptCore/bytecode/UnlinkedCodeBlock.h:414), which the VM's CodeCache shares
  between evaluations of the same source in any global object. The code reads its CodeBlock's
  data through two registers it loads at entry, the JIT data (constants, inline caches) and the
  metadata table (jit/JIT.cpp:653-658); constants are a pool indexed at run time (JITConstantPool,
  jit/BaselineJITCode.h:60-85). A few operations make a function's code unshareable
  (m_isShareable, jit/JITOpcodes.cpp:1895, 1994). WebKit main, fetched 2026-11-04.
- V8 compiles bytecode once per source and isolate: the compilation cache's script table maps a
  source to its SharedFunctionInfo (CompilationCacheScript::Lookup and Put,
  src/codegen/compilation-cache.h:48-59), and the code cache serializes compiled bytecode for an
  embedder to load instead of compiling (CodeSerializer::Serialize and Deserialize,
  src/snapshot/code-serializer.h:191-222), as Node does for its own JavaScript; Sparkplug's code is
  per isolate, compiled from that bytecode in one pass. V8 main, fetched 2026-11-05.
- SpiderMonkey shares a script's immutable data, its bytecode included, among the scripts that
  compile the same source, by reference count through a table (SharedImmutableScriptData,
  js/src/vm/SharedStencil.h:636-660, "each pointer from a JSScript counts as one reference plus
  there may be one reference from the shared script data table"). Firefox main, fetched 2026-11-05.

Two tiers of remedy, to be designed in this order:
1. Cheaper compiles a page makes anyway: the compact templates (designed above; every first-stage
   byte they shed is shed on every page) and region code only where a function has run (the
   phase exit's candidates: a recompile when hot), since region spans are most of a large
   function's bytes (Djot's census: 2.30 of 3.96 MB).
2. Reuse, as JSC's: a function's first-stage machine code compiled once per process for its
   bytecode identity (a static snapshot's function, a script's by its source) and shared by every
   heap that runs it, reading its per-heap data through ctx as JSC's baseline reads its
   CodeBlock's. What first-stage code embeds today, by the emitters' immediates (jit*.rs): the
   site's cache cells (mov_imm64 of cache_ptr, at every property, call, name and element site),
   static name addresses (Decision 21: environment slots by address), atom words (key-checked
   reads, PropKey::from_text), environment pointers, the epoch cells (process-wide already) and,
   in second-stage code only, baked shapes. Bytecode chunks would split as JSC's UnlinkedCodeBlock
   from CodeBlock and SpiderMonkey's stencil from its script: the ops, constants' descriptions and
   the code, shared; the caches, constants' values and environment homes, per heap.

Scope (proposed, the owner's to decide): tier 1 in P2, with the compact templates (designed and
approved; queued behind Vue's Proxy reads) and a design for region code only where a function has
run; tier 2 in P3. Tier 2 is a change to every first-stage emitter (each per-heap immediate read
through ctx instead) and to the bytecode chunk (Chunk, bytecode.rs:2845-3136: its ops and
constants' descriptions shared, its caches, values and code slot per heap), which is a phase's
work, and it is what lets the threshold drop (t1a2: Djot -9.5%, React -3.2% on the fixtures'
timers) without TRust's pages paying for it. A measured intermediate, if wanted in P2: the bytecode
shared alone, which a page's bytecode compiles bound at a quarter of its compile time on the
event-loop page (4.6 of about 19 ms).

Addendum to W6 step 2b's record (2026-11-05): lib GC stress at 4fc709f2 (landed as 7b2afa56) with
TRUST_JS_GC_STRESS=1000, TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=force and TRUST_JS_GC_VERIFY=1, each of 663 tests
in its own process (W6's selection with 2b's: gc_cycle_tests and the table_record_tests that run
cycles, both closure-check should_panic tests among them): 662 pass. The one that fails,
memory::tests::temporal_records_account_zone_and_calendar_strings_once, fails under stress on main
before W6 as well. releasing_long_object_chains_uses_bounded_native_stack took 2,963 s; the
known-slow integer_comparisons_and_branches_match_in_every_tier was left out
(target/p2/w6/impl/stress/run-4fc709f2-force/results.txt).

### W6 step 3: precleaning (record draft, 2026-11-05)

Commit, from main 83a24a43, on p2-w6 (an agent's; worktree target/p2/w6-impl-wt), landed on main
as e8cd037d over a53f1903 (main's commits since 83a24a43 change only this plan; the code is
f63528c2's):
- f63528c2: with TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL, a marking cycle precleans (design 5). Each time a
  slice's drain runs out of work, the marked cells whose cards are set, written since their
  trace, go back to the worklist for full traces, which the next slices do while the program
  runs, and the cards are cleared (Heap::preclean). Precleaning repeats until a round, a
  preclean and the drain of what its cells reach, finds fewer than 7,000 such cells and traces
  under 1 MiB (PRECLEAN_DONE_CELLS, PRECLEAN_DONE_BYTES, provisional until the schedule, step 4:
  the design's 0.5 ms of rescan at TypeScript's 67-78 ns a cell, and about 0.5 ms of marking);
  the final pause follows once the worklist runs out after such a round, and rescans only the
  cells written since.
  - Not on a timer: a preclean comes only when the worklist runs out (design 5: a program's hot
    cells would be rescanned at every preclean).
  - The final pause's rescan and the preclean take the cards the same way
    (Heap::take_cycle_card_cells: every page's marked cells on set cards, for full traces).
  - The GC log: `[gc-slice]` lines add the cycle's precleans so far and the cells the last one
    found (`precleans`, `precleaned`); a major collection's `[gc-heap]` line adds the marked cells
    its final pause rescanned for their cards (`card_cells`, 0 for a major collection in one
    pause). DIAGNOSTICS.md describes precleaning and the fields.
  - No change to the barrier, the allocator, either JIT backend or a collection's marking in one
    pause.

Where the build differs from the design:
1. A round ends precleaning by what its drain traced as well as by the cells its preclean found.
   The design's rule (repeat until a preclean finds fewer cells than the final pause's budget)
   left a SplayLatency final pause at 62 ms in a first build: the cycle's one preclean found 282
   cells, whose drain took 150 slices and 40 MB, since Splay's rotations move subtrees the
   marker had not reached under nodes it had, and meanwhile the program moved 63 MB more behind
   1,371 written cells for the final pause to trace. With the drain's bytes in the rule its
   cycles take 6 to 10 precleans and its final pauses 0.4-1.9 ms (impl/prof/s3).

Tests: gc_core: a store into a traced cell during a cycle, rescanned by the preclean when the
worklist runs out (what it stored is marked before the final pause, which rescans no card), and
precleaning repeated while a preclean finds at least its budget (two precleans: one that finds
the cells written, one that finds none, then the final pause with no card to rescan).

### W6 step 3's fix: a preclean flushes the allocation cursors first (record, 2026-11-05)

7ead16a2 (p2-w6-s3fix, an agent's, on main 0ffdedcb; landed by fast-forward). A use-after-free
on main e8cd037d (step 3) to this fix with TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL on, the cycle off by default:
a preclean takes a young page's cards by walking its marked cells up to the page's next_unused,
which only a cursor's move to another bitmap word or a flush (a collection's start, the final
pause) brings up to date; slices never flushed, so a cell allocated in the cursor's current word
since its last refill, traced by the cycle and then written by the program, was skipped while its
card was cleared, and the final pause swept what only its new edge reached (Octane TypeScript
crashed once in about 36 runs of steps 3 and 4: SEGV_MAPERR in Object::trace_gc_fields at a task
boundary's collection). The fix: Heap::preclean calls flush_cursors() first (the final pause's
final_marking already flushed). Test:
a_preclean_rescans_a_written_cell_allocated_since_the_cursors_were_flushed builds exactly that
cell; it fails on main and passes with the fix. Why the gates missed it: allocation under
TRUST_JS_GC_STRESS takes the slow path, which flushes at every allocation, so next_unused was never
stale under stress; under force the unit tests precleaned rarely; and the cycle on at
TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=1 ran only in release builds, without verification. Checks at 7ead16a2:
lib 2,815/2,815 by default and under force; clippy -D warnings x3; zombie 2,596 and clippy x3;
the Test262 subset under force, stress 100 (every 2nd major) and verification 2,603/2,603 in both
tiers; 18 TypeScript runs with the cycle on without a crash (the diagnosis rests on the core dump
and the test). The verification that would have caught it follows as its own commit (the next
record): forced precleaning at every slice end, checks where the class begins (no cell past the
young walk's bound; each cycle take of the cards against a walk of the page's marks under
TRUST_JS_GC_VERIFY), and a gate run of Test262 under force with verification and small budgets,
no stress, so allocation takes the fast path as in production (75 tests catch the unfixed code).
The every-slice barrier walk (the coordinator's first proposal) was measured and not taken: it is
quadratic under force (the 44 cycle tests 929 s against 4.2 s), caught nothing beyond the sampled
walk on the unfixed code, and no exemplar verifies after every increment (V8's
FullMarkingVerifier once marking has finished, src/heap/mark-compact.cc:840-847; SpiderMonkey's
IncrementalMarkingValidator as marking ends, js/src/gc/Sweeping.cpp:2004-2005, its pre-barrier
verifier sampled, js/src/gc/Verifier.cpp:468-486; JSC's verifyGC once marking has finished,
heap/Collector.cpp:716-719).

### W6 step 3's fix: verification that catches a card cleared without its cell (record, 2026-11-05)

7052d909 (p2-w6-s3fix, an agent's, on main 76647c1d, landed by fast-forward; 91944e3b before the
rebase, the same engine tree, on which the checks and counts ran). Design 11's verification, made to catch the class of
step 3's preclean bug (the previous record) where it begins:
- Under TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=force every slice ends with a preclean (Heap::run_slice), so that
  precleaning runs as often as slicing, in every state of the marking and of the allocation
  cursors; before, a forced slice precleaned only once its worklist ran out after a round that
  was not small.
- A young page's take of its cards asserts (debug builds) its walk's precondition: no cell
  allocated in a word past next_unused, the walk's bound (PageMeta::take_card_cells). Every
  caller flushes the cursors first; the unfixed preclean broke it at most takes.
- With heap verification, each take of the cards in a cycle, a preclean's and the final pause's
  (Heap::take_cycle_card_cells), is checked against a walk over its page's marks: the cells taken
  are the page's marked cells whose cards are set, in address order
  (PageMeta::take_card_cells_checked).
- The barrier check's walk over the heap stays sampled under force, as on main and as
  SpiderMonkey samples its barrier verifier (the previous record gives the measurements and the
  exemplars).
- Test taking_the_cards_past_an_unflushed_cursor_panics (debug builds): a cycle's take of the
  cards with a cell allocated past an unflushed cursor's page bound panics at the take.
- DIAGNOSTICS.md: force's slices each end with a preclean; the checked takes.

The unfixed code caught:
- 91944e3b without the fix's flush (target/p2/w6/impl/src-ver-nofix): the 45 cycle tests fail 4,
  each at the bound's assertion (the fix's regression test,
  a_cycle_keeps_what_the_program_reaches_through_its_slices_in_every_tier,
  weak_collections_keep_their_live_entries_across_a_cycle_in_every_tier,
  a_weak_maps_entries_are_discovered_in_the_slices_and_merged_at_the_final_pause_in_every_tier);
  the Test262 subset under force and verification without stress at small budgets 2,528/2,603
  (75 caught: 60 panics, 15 aborts where a panic cannot unwind); under stress 100 (every 2nd
  major) 2,603/2,603, as expected (stress flushes at every allocation).
- e8cd037d with each check behind a switch (impl/src-e8x; logs impl/logs/e8x and
  impl/t262stress/e8x-*), beyond the fix's regression test, which fails there:
  - The 44 cycle unit tests (gc_core's cycle tests, gc_cycle_tests, table_record): main's
    verification 0; forced precleans 0; forced precleans with the walk after every slice 0 (in
    681 s); the bound check 1; forced precleans with the bound check 3
    (a_cycle_keeps_what_the_program_reaches_through_its_slices_in_every_tier,
    weak_collections_keep_their_live_entries_across_a_cycle_in_every_tier,
    a_weak_maps_entries_are_discovered_in_the_slices_and_merged_at_the_final_pause_in_every_tier).
  - The Test262 subset (13 directories, 2,603 tests) under force and verification without stress
    at small budgets (TRUST_JS_GC_NURSERY_BYTES=0, TRUST_JS_GC_MIN_HEAP_BYTES=1,
    TRUST_JS_GC_PACING=0), default tier: main's verification 2,603/2,603; forced precleans
    2,603/2,603; forced precleans with the bound check 2,528/2,603 (75 caught: 60 panics, 15
    aborts where a panic cannot unwind). Under stress 100 (every 2nd major) with both:
    2,603/2,603, as expected (stress flushes at every allocation).

### Vue's Proxy reads, step 1: arguments rooted by their frames, not the registry (record, 2026-11-05)

Branch p2-proxy, on main 2c430516 (whose engine is 88067f94's: the base binary is that build,
target/p2/proxy/lto/main-88067f94). Two commits, each measured against its parent.

3df22f51, the first part: CallbackCache::call takes its arguments as an array of the caller's
own, words of the native frame for the whole call, its polls and its tail drain, where the
conservative stack scan roots them (Decision 0), as Interp::call_getter's window and
Callback::call's prepared entry already were; it no longer enters them in the rooting registry.
Every Proxy trap's call comes this way (Interp::proxy_call_trap), and so do Callback::call's calls
before their callee is prepared. call_values, whose slice may be Rust-heap storage, keeps its
registration.

1d242967, the second part (approved with the design note): the native-call boundary
(Interp::call_native_committed_with) no longer registers its window; its callers root the receiver
and the window for the whole call. Every native call from generated code reaches the boundary on
its record's operands: the call-hit helper (jit_call_hit), the generic call helpers (jit_call,
jit_exec's Call and CallWithThis), and the spread call, whose arguments are in a native-stack
buffer. The Rust callers, all through Interp::call_jit_cached and Interp::call_prepared, already had
to root their windows by those functions' contracts: CallbackCache::call (the first part),
call_values (its registration), call_getter and call_setter (native-stack windows). The two tests
that called the boundary from Rust on an unregistered Rust-heap window register it themselves
(jit::rooting_tests' committed_from_rust; scope_tests' committed scoped loan), as such a caller now
must.

Why generated code's window is a root for the whole call. A native called from generated code
reads its arguments in place, in the calling activation's operand words. That activation runs on
a pooled record (jit::JitFrame), which the collector traces from the pop that starts the activation
to the push or free that ends it, scanning all of its FRAME_BUF words (slots and operands)
conservatively, without a stack pointer; an activation too large for a record runs on a Rust
entry's buffer, which it registers for its whole run (gc_trace::JitFrameRoots, words: the slots and
the whole operand buffer). The caller's activation is suspended in the helper for the whole native
call: it does not end, so its record or buffer stays traced through the native, every safepoint and
collection inside it (allocation, polls, GC stress's collections), any reentry (a callback, a getter,
a nested native: each runs on records and buffers of its own, so none writes the caller's words),
the post-call interrupt poll and the pending-tail drain, which the boundary runs before returning.
The window is immutable meanwhile: the boundary lends it as a slice and the caller retires those
operand positions only after the boundary returns. A receiver-less call's `this` is a local
Undefined on the helper's native frame. The spread call's buffer is an array on the helper's native
frame, which the conservative scan roots until the helper returns. The rooting tests already showed
the record's scan at work: a native called at a warmed site marks its receiver and argument by roots
(jit::rooting_tests::committed_native_call_operands_are_roots, "RR"), which now holds with the
boundary's registration gone.

### Vue's Proxy reads, step 2: property-key strings carry their key (record, 2026-11-05)

7cece2de on p2-proxy (after step 1's 1d242967), Fork 5 as decided. A string that is the value of
one property key carries that key's word in its frontier, the header word an exact string never
uses (an in-place append needs the string to end at its buffer's frontier), with the word's top
bit as the mark (lstr::KEY_MARK). ToPropertyKey of such a string is then a load, a test and a mask
(PropKey::of_marked), as V8's ToName of an internalized string, SpiderMonkey's AtomizeString of an
atom and JSC's toIdentifier of an atom string return the key at once. The marked strings:
- every heap atom, from its making (AtomTable::insert): its own key, or an index's for index text
  (an atom of "17" is the key 17); text that begins with NUL is a Symbol's key or an escaped one,
  whose value is another string, and carries none;
- each heap's one copy of each static name it uses as a value (atom::static_name_string, kept with
  the heap's interned strings for its life, after the ASCII units and the index strings), the
  decision's one permanent marked copy per heap, as JSC keeps its common identifiers per VM; it
  replaces the property_key_strings LRU for static names;
- the canonical index strings below 1,024 (jstr::index_lstr), which replace the LRU for those
  indices.
property_key_string returns these, so a Proxy trap's key, and every key value made of an atom, a
static name or a small index, is marked. A Proxy read makes its key value from the key the read
already holds (Interp::key_value_of, through get_member_recv_impl's atom) rather than its text.
The readers: Reflect.get (get_named_cached takes the key), the in operator and Reflect.has
(ordinary_chain_has_key seeds the walk's atom), and computed reads by a String key (their cache
miss). A map that has the key in hand now compares key words at any size (Props::find_text_with),
where a small map compared each key's text. That lookup is out of line (Props::find_out_of_line):
inlined into find_text_with, which every map walk inlines, it moved x86-64's code for EarleyBoyer's
hot loops (+0.24% there in 48ab68bc, this step's first version; 7cece2de amends it to +0.00%,
measured with variants without the key-word lookup, varA, and with it out of line, varD).

Measured (fat LTO against 1d242967, CPUs 10-13, setarch -R, pacing off, median of 3).

Micros, instructions an iteration (the difference of the 1.2M- and 200k-iteration runs over 1M;
micro/s2s3-final.txt and the `in` loops' run):

| loop body | step 1 | step 2 | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `p.x`, trap `get(t, k, r) { return Reflect.get(t, k, r); }` | 2,499.3 | 2,297.3 | -8.1% |

The trap's key now carries its key: the trap's own Reflect.get and `t[k]` take it without a lookup
of its text (-202 and -112 a read). A literal is not an atom and carries no key, so the last loops
with a literal pay the test of the mark and the text's lookup as before (3 to 14 instructions; the
`in` and Reflect.has paths' inlining moved too). V8 internalizes literals; making the compiler's
string constants atoms would mark them, though for a one-key map the text compare costs about what
the key-word lookup does (545 and 548 above).

### Vue's Proxy reads, step 3: a named read's Proxy trap called from the read's helper stub (record, 2026-11-05)

cd271daa on p2-proxy (after step 2's 7cece2de), the design note's forks 1 to 4 as decided. Its
measured binaries were built from fb766b90, whose engine code it is (cd271daa only counts the new
interpreter field in the memory-inventory test). A named read whose receiver is a Proxy (ECMA-262
§10.5.8 [[Get]], the Proxy the Receiver) runs through the read's own Proxy caches, as Decision 17's
getters run through the read's getter call cache: a chunk's trap table (bytecode::TrapTable), keyed
by the read's pc as the getter table is, holds for each read its form and implicit position, the
property cache that finds `get` on the handler, the trap's call cache, the key's value (a String
that carries its key, step 2, and lives as long as the heap) and a flag set while the read's
handlers have no `get` (bytecode::TrapGet).

The helper (jit_get_prop, both backends) answers a Proxy receiver where the read's property cache
has declined it (Interp::get_prop_ic_from_slot's declined branch, given the read's chunk and pc; the
receiver's kind tag read in place), so that no other read pays for it: the read's slot, made at its
first Proxy receiver (the form from the read's operation), marks the read's property cache generic
as the cache's refused fill did (W4 step 5's mark) and answers the read (Interp::proxy_get_cached):
GetMethod(handler, "get") through the slot's property cache; the trap through the slot's call cache,
which a compiled trap's call fills, on (target, key, receiver) kept in the helper's native frame; a
revoked handler, an absent or a non-callable `get` keep their errors and the target's [[Get]]. A
slot's call cache keeps its own pins of the callees its ways record by identity
(bytecode::TrapCalls), which every collection prunes as a callback cache's
(Interp::gc_prune_dead_pins, through Interp::trap_calls): a way whose callee died forgets that
identity and keeps its function and code, which another closure of the function matches by code.

On ARM64 the reads' helper stub (H_GET_PROP), after its accessor test, probes the read's slot by pc
(jit::emit_get_prop_trap): a read whose handlers had no `get` takes the helper at once; otherwise
the receiver, as the slot's form places it, must be a Proxy (kind tag KIND_PROXY_TAG) whose handler
is an Object; `get` is read from the handler by the property way loop on the slot's cache, at any
depth (a data property; an accessor or an absence takes the helper); the trap is found in the slot's
call cache by identity in way 0 or by code in the CallSecondary stub (which matches chai's per-proxy
closures); and the direct sequence runs it on [handler, trap, target, key, receiver] above the
operands. Every frame keeps room for that window (jit_ir::trap_window, five words above a named
read's incoming depth). The trap frame records the read's position; a throw is placed at the read
(jit_accessor_threw).

The invariant (step 10) after the trap, Fork 4: a property layout keeps a sticky flag
(value::PropertyLayoutData::validates), set where a key gets attributes that constrain a trap's
result (non-configurable, and read-only data or an accessor), as SpiderMonkey's
NeedsProxyGetSetResultValidation and JSC's hasNonConfigurableReadOnlyOrGetterSetterProperties. A
target that is an ordinary object or an Array, ic_plain, whose layout's flag is clear needs no
check: the stub tests its kind, its flag byte and its layout's byte; Rust tests the same before
looking the key up (proxy_invariant_vacuous, which the Rust paths of every trap share). Any other
target is checked in Rust (bytecode::jit_proxy_get_checked from the stub), which also catches a trap
that made the target's property non-configurable during the call.

The first versions and the amendments. db43d1e0 tested every read that reached the helper for a
Proxy receiver before its property cache (a borrow and a tag compare in each of the four forms'
arms), and its trap call caches pinned their callees in the chunk's call pins, which outlive their
ways. Its counts (fat LTO against 7cece2de): ARM64 Vue -8.71%, but chai +0.36%, Gameboy +1.12%,
PdfJS +0.31%, TypeScript +0.21%; x86-64 Vue -0.60%, chai +2.86%, DeltaBlue +1.92%, TypeScript
+1.73%, Box2D +1.37%, RayTrace +1.23%, RegExp +0.93%, Richards +0.91%, React +0.88%, Djot +0.85%
(counts/s3-db43d1e0.txt, zombie/counts-s3c.txt). Gameboy's 18.2M helper reads (13.1M answered by the
Rust property cache, 5.1M typed arrays) paid the test (+472 samples of 500,009 instructions:
get_named_property_from_slot +245, get_prop_ic_impl +193, the moved inlining's memcmp calls +224).
a2b4df2b moved the test to the declined branch and gave each slot its own pins, pruned to its ways
at each call: ARM64 Vue -8.69%, chai -0.80%, Gameboy +0.17%, PdfJS +0.34%, TypeScript +0.10%, the
rest within 0.04% (counts/s3e-a2b4df2b.txt); but x86-64 kept its regressions (React +0.93%,
DeltaBlue +1.67%, Box2D +1.41%, chai +2.01%, Vue +0.31%; zombie/counts-s3e.txt). Box2D's profile put
them in the slot read helper itself (get_named_property_from_slot +8% of its own samples,
jit_get_prop +11%): the form had become its seventh argument, which x86-64 passes on the stack, and
the receiver's form a load and spill on every read. And chai's collections, on x86-64 and on ARM64
with in-line stubs (the Rust path for every read), still spent five to nine times as long in the
weak-cell pass (x86-64 1.34 s against 0.15 s): a fill-counting variant found only 31k fills for 2.1M
trap reads, so the cost was not new pins but the dead closures the ways' pins kept reserved, which
every collection re-pins (gc_handle.rs: a dead target's cell stays young). cd271daa passes the
helper its six arguments again (the slot's form comes from the read's operation when the slot is
made), tests a String receiver before the name in the length shortcut, answers a slot's later reads
before making its key value, and prunes the slots' pins at each collection.

### Vue's Proxy reads, step 4: Reflect.get, has and set answered on their operands (record, 2026-11-05)

2905c4c4 on p2-proxy (after step 3's cd271daa), Fork 6 as decided: option (a), V8's baseline. A
call of Reflect.get, Reflect.has or Reflect.set whose call cache proves the native (its class,
bytecode::INTRINSIC_REFLECT_GET, _HAS and _SET, declared with the natives' templates), from
generated code (jit_call_hit, through Interp::call_native_light) or from a call cache of the
interpreter's (Interp::call_native_entry), is answered on the caller's operand window without
the native call when its resolution runs no author code (Interp::reflect_resolved), as V8's
optimizing tiers call GetPropertyWithReceiver and HasProperty directly
(src/compiler/js-call-reducer.cc:3855-3943; src/maglev/maglev-graph-builder.cc:10696-10727): a
target that is an Object and a key that is a String carrying its key (step 2: an atom, a static
name's copy, a small index), so the key is never looked up by its text. Anything else takes the
native, through the boundary, as before. The three classes join the native classes' one match
(bytecode::native_operands for the hit, native_entry_class for the interpreter's caches), so no
other native's call pays for them, where a first version (dbcffe1a) tested for them before that
match.

- Reflect.get (§28.1.5) reads a data property, whose value does not depend on the Receiver,
  through the stub cache by the receiver's shape and the key (a re-derivation fills it: the
  same resolution as get_named_cached's, without its getter call), an Array's `length`, or an
  own plain element; a getter, an exotic object on the chain or a name the ICs leave to [[Get]]
  (index-like or NUL-led text, `description`, long text) takes the native.
- Reflect.has (§28.1.9) walks a chain of ordinary objects and Arrays by the key
  (ordinary_chain_has_key) or finds an own element; a hole, a far index or another object on
  the chain takes the native.
- Reflect.set (§28.1.13) writes where OrdinarySet's steps on the Receiver are the target's own
  (Interp::reflect_set_receiver_forwards): no receiver, the target, or a Proxy of the target
  whose handler has neither a `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` nor a `defineProperty` trap (§10.5.5
  step 7 and §10.5.6 step 7 forward those to the target), found by the property ICs on an
  ordinary handler's chain without author code; Vue's set trap passes its Proxy so
  (`Reflect.set(target, key, value, receiver)`), as the census's 23,781 four-argument calls show.
  The write: the store IC's resolution with a scratch cache (try_ic_set: an own writable data
  property, or a creation the chain allows on an extensible target), an element (fast_set_elem:
  an overwrite, an append), or an Array's writable `length` (ArraySetLength of a Number that is
  a valid length). A read-only property, a setter, a non-extensible target, an invalid length,
  a typed array or any other receiver takes the native.

V8, SpiderMonkey and JSC answer Reflect.set with a generic C++ builtin, which looks the receiver's
traps up when it is a Proxy: V8's ReflectSet calls Object::SetSuperProperty
(src/builtins/builtins-reflect.cc:72-97), whose JSPROXY receiver case asks the Proxy's
GetOwnPropertyDescriptor and then defines (src/objects/objects.cc:2673-2690); SpiderMonkey's
Reflect_set (js/src/builtin/Reflect.cpp:135) reaches SetPropertyByDefining
(js/src/vm/NativeObject.cpp:2512); JSC's reflectObjectSet reaches definePropertyOnReceiver, whose
Proxy receiver takes definePropertyOnReceiverSlow (Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSObject.cpp:967,
999-1016). The resolution here is that algorithm on the key in hand, where the Proxy has neither
trap, without the native call's machinery.

A literal key is not an atom and carries no key: `Reflect.get(t, 'x')` still takes the native (the
micros' reflget and reflhas rows); the traps' keys and every key a property enumeration gives back
carry theirs (reflgetk, reflhask, reflsetk).

### Compact baseline templates, step 1: first-stage property reads through a shared stub (record, 2026-11-05)

9c67bd05 on p2-compact (from main a3fd64da; an agent's), landed on main as c50a0b4e over 9deaece0
(main's commits since a3fd64da change only this plan; the code is 9c67bd05's), the design's item 2 ("Compact baseline templates
(census, survey and design, 2026-11-04)"). A named read (GetProp, GetPropThis, GetPropLocal,
GetMethod) outside loops (use_shared_stub's rule: shared stubs on and the site not in a loop
body) whose cache gave its compile no way to bake, which is every read of a function's first
native code (its caches are empty when the first native compile runs, at its first bytecode run),
keeps in line only:
- the receiver's load (the operand, ctx.this_word or the local) and its object-tag test, the
  payload into x10; a read that probes a primitive's wrapper prototype (wrap_ok) leaves its
  receiver word in x9 for the stub instead;
- a String's `length` (emit_ascii_string_length), as before;
- the cache's address in x8 and, for a key-checked read, the site's key word in x6 (an atom's
  address, which lives as long as the heap the code belongs to, or a tagged index);
- the call of the shared stub, a branch on its answer, and the helper's stub call
  (emit_op_helper H_GET_PROP), as the in-line template's slow path.

The stub (jit::SharedStub::PropRead, emit_prop_read_stub; one per combination of the probe's
flags, Array receiver, wrapper receiver, method and key-checked, and of whether the read pushes
its value or replaces the receiver operand, and of the `prototype` guard) runs what every site
carried: the wrapper receiver's dispatch (emit_packed_probe_receiver, now a function the in-line
template shares), the way loop (emit_prop_way_loop), the landings (the slot's bounds and word, the
accessor test and the publication of a validated accessor for the helper, the deferred `prototype`
guard, the key-checked arm comparing x6, a cached absence) and the commit. It returns w9 = 1 when
the value is in place, 2 for a cached absence's `undefined` (a test build's site tells the two
apart for its property events), 0 for the helper with every operand as it was. Process-wide: no
per-heap word is in it; the key word is the site's. The read's helper stub is the one Proxy step 3
reshaped: a declined read publishes a validated accessor or not, as before, and the helper stub
tries the getter's direct call, then the Proxy trap's, then the helper.

Second-stage code (seeded with the warm caches, which bakes their ways), loop bodies and a
`TRUST_JS_JIT_INLINE_STUBS` build keep the in-line template.

The exemplars: V8's Sparkplug calls a builtin for every named read with feedback
(LoadICBaseline; baseline/baseline-compiler.cc:1071-1083), SpiderMonkey's Baseline calls the
site's IC stub, compiled once per zone and shared by every site that attaches the same CacheIR
(BaselineCacheIRCompiler.cpp:2058-2108), and JSC's Baseline runs the shared handler its data IC
names (JITPropertyAccess.cpp:548-580).

### W6 step 4: the schedule (record, 2026-11-05)

49928c01, 0e95a5c4, 7b312b1d, 5504ace9 (p2-w6-s4-fmt, an agent's; worktree target/p2/w6-impl-wt), on main
a3fd64da (the Proxy series and the formatting commit), landed on main over 2e99ccba as 2af3bfee,
9dda3c1a, 565a5929 and 20d51071: the code is 5504ace9's plus compact templates' step 1 (c50a0b4e),
line for line, and that combined tree's ARM64 lib suite passed by default and under
TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=force (2,829 passed each, the formerly quadratic test included) before main
moved. With TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL (off by default), V8's schedule for
a marking cycle:
- The start, at V8's soft limit: a minor collection whose sweep leaves the room below the byte
  budget at one nursery's budget or less makes a major collection due, which starts a cycle (V8
  starts marking once the room below its old generation's limit is a young generation's capacity
  or less, src/heap/heap.cc:5620-5671; Heap::major_due_bytes). Without incremental marking, the
  budget as before.
- The floor: a major collection the heap asks for marks in one pause while the heap holds 8 MB
  or less, in release builds, V8's activation threshold (8 MB in release builds and 0 in debug
  builds, src/heap/incremental-marking.cc:62-68, 135-138; MIN_CYCLE_HEAP_BYTES); the forced mode
  (verification's) has none.
- A slice's work: the bytes behind the larger of two expectations and at least 64 KB, V8's step
  when marking makes no progress (Heap::slice_bytes): V8's time schedule, the bytes the cycle
  started with marked over 500 ms (src/heap/base/incremental-marking-schedule.h:40-56,
  .cc:99-130), and an allocation schedule, those bytes marked once the cycle has allocated half
  its room before the margin (design 4), so that it ends before the margin when the program
  allocates fast. Slices come every 64 KB allocated, as before.
- Its time: at most 1 ms, V8's step from a task (src/heap/incremental-marking.cc:56-60): the
  drain reads the clock every 128 cells it traces and every 128 conditional edges it fires
  (SLICE_CLOCK_CELLS; V8's marking reads it every 128 objects, src/heap/mark-compact.cc:2296,
  2360-2365). A preclean's pass over the pages stops at the slice's deadline too, read every 16
  pages, and the next slice resumes it (Cycle::preclean_page).
- Pacing: a major collection's speed is its marked bytes over its cycle's whole marking time,
  the slices' and the final pause's (Pacing::cycle_marked), V8's combined speed
  (OldGenerationSpeedInBytesPerMillisecond, src/heap/gc-tracer.cc:1359-1389); the cycle's slices
  are timed whenever the heap paces (Heap::cycle_clock). Under TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=force, the
  final pause's alone: forced slices of a few cells, each with a preclean and checks, time the
  verification, and made the memory reducer find the allocation rate high (its older test,
  the_memory_reducer_collects_a_quiet_heap_after_a_major_collection_left_it_large, re-armed
  instead of collecting under force).
- The memory reducer starts a cycle instead of collecting (the owner's decision 7; V8's starts
  incremental marking, src/heap/memory-reducer.cc:92-105); its final pause reduces memory as the
  collection did.
- Idle slices: Engine::advance_incremental_marking runs a slice, or the final pause once nothing
  is left (V8's incremental marking job, src/heap/incremental-marking-job.cc:80-137, each task a
  step), and Engine::incremental_marking_running says whether to. The runtime's event loop calls
  it while it waits for a timer or a task, beside the memory reducer (trust-js-runtime's
  run_to_completion).
- The GC log's line for a cycle's start gives the heap's phases (begin, roots, stack, side, drain).
- DIAGNOSTICS.md describes the start, the floor, the schedule, the idle slices and the start
  line's phases.

Where the build differs from the design:
- Decision 7 had the engine report the cycle's next slice deadline beside the memory reducer's,
  for the runtime's loop to run a slice when due. Built without a deadline: while a cycle runs its
  next step is due at once, as V8's job posts each step's task without a delay and posts the next
  after each step (src/heap/incremental-marking-job.cc:53-70, 127-135). The loop runs slices back
  to back while no timer is due, each pass first running whatever became runnable.
- Design 5 precleans once the worklist empties; with the 1 ms cap a pass over the pages cannot
  always finish in one slice (TypeScript's precleans take hundreds of thousands of cells), so it
  stops at the deadline and the next slice resumes it from the page where it stopped; the cycle's
  marking is complete only once a whole pass found no written cell.
- The drain's clock also counts the conditional edges it fires: a side-slot owner's slots can
  take long to trace.
- Under TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL=force the combined speed counts the final pause alone (the lib
  suite under force found the reducer re-arming instead of collecting); two tests that assumed
  one-pause collections changed: the reducer's older test lets idle steps finish its cycles, and
  replaced_arrays_are_collected_as_their_elements_grow pins incremental marking off (a cycle that
  starts at the soft limit takes the element blocks' charges toward its margin, and its count of
  collections, 8 under force, fell below the test's 10).

Commits after the schedule (each its own, for the coordinator's decisions):
- 0e95a5c4: the allocation schedule counts the cycle's own allocation (approved by the coordinator).
- 7b312b1d: a forced slice precleans a part of a pass (approved), FORCED_PRECLEAN_PAGES (16) pages that the
  next slices resume, instead of a whole pass: verification's forced precleans (7052d909)
  re-traced a cell the program writes at every safepoint at every slice, and a growing array's
  owner traces all its words, so the lib suite's live_object_limit_error_handler_can_allocate
  ran over 30 minutes under force (220 s without the forced precleans; 623 s with 16 pages, 250
  s with 1). Without the fix's flush, the 16-page passes catch the unfixed preclean in the same 4
  cycle tests and 69 Test262 tests at small budgets (75 with whole passes, 37 with 1 page).

The allocation schedule's estimate (0e95a5c4): the allocation schedule asked for the bytes at the
cycle's start, marked by half its room; with white allocation the cycle's survivors are marking
work too, and V8's estimate leaves its young generation out (its TODO to count it,
src/heap/incremental-marking.cc:686-687), while a cycle here runs no minor collection, so all
its allocation is of that kind. On CPU 5 under the hold: Splay's final pause 11.54 ms (10.62 ms
of drain, the cycle forced at its margin after 29.7 MB) became 0.38 ms (complete after 14.6 MB);
TypeScript's largest final 26.30 ms (forced after 55.5 MB) 7.64 ms (complete; 3.22 ms of it the
sweep's free, step 5's); SplayLatency's driver's first final 7.66 ms (forced) 0.43 ms.

The cycle's start, V8's (5504ace9; the coordinator's decision on a fork): design 6 had the
start clear the marks and cards, mark the roots and the native stack, register the side tables'
edges and run a first slice. V8's start (StartMarkingMajor, src/heap/incremental-marking.cc:
247-324) marks the roots without the stack (MarkRoots, :221-228, SkipRoot::kStack) and runs no
step: its first step is the job's task (:320-323). SpiderMonkey marks the stack as it starts
(traceRuntimeCommon, js/src/gc/RootMarking.cpp:314-331, from beginMarkPhase, js/src/gc/GC.cpp:
3350, 3439) because its snapshot-at-the-beginning barrier needs it; JSC scans it at every stop
(the "Cs" constraint, heap/Heap.cpp:2378-2427). TRust's barrier is V8's kind, the final pause
marking every root and the stack again, so the start now marks the roots alone and runs no slice,
and no longer zeroes the stack below its frames (which served the scan). On CPU 5 the stack and
the first slice had been 10-34% of every start, 0.10-0.35 ms:

| workload | start (ms) | stack | first slice |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TypeScript | 1.76 | 0.12 | 0.06 |
| chai | 2.34 | 0.15 | 0.11 |
| PdfJS | 1.16 | 0.21 | 0.08 |
| Gameboy | 1.02 | 0.09 | 0.26 |
| EarleyBoyer | 0.91 | 0.07 | 0.07 |
| SplayLatency's driver | 1.17 | 0.05 | 0.07 |

Sustained allocation's 2.80 ms start was its first slice's 2.57 ms, one array's whole block (V8
scans large arrays in chunks, MarkingProgressTracker, src/heap/marking-visitor-inl.h:618-690),
which moves to the next slice: the large blocks are measured after step 4 (the design's order).
Two tests that took the start's slice for granted run one or two slices first, and
the_memory_reducer_collects_a_quiet_heap_after_a_major_collection_left_it_large lets the idle
steps finish the cycle the reducer starts under TRUST_JS_GC_INCREMENTAL (in 49928c01, the commit that
makes the reducer start one).

### W6 step 5: the spare pages' release out of the final pause (record, 2026-11-05)

e50f5725 (p2-w6-s5-wip, an agent's, on main cccf7545; landed by fast-forward).

What the pause spends: SplayLatency's driver's late final pauses (16.7 and 15.1 ms with step 4
on CPU 5) were 14.3 and 12.3 ms of untimed sweep work. A probe around Heap::trim_spare_pages (a
non-LTO build of 51cabcde, CPU 3) times it: one final pause gave 2,228 spare pages back (2,740
down to the cap of 512), 139 MB, in 10.3 ms, about 4.6 us a page (os_pages::discard, one madvise
each); the pause was 14.6 ms with 11.0 ms of the engine's sweep. The cycle-off majors pay it too
(splay-real's last, 112.9 ms, has 10.1 ms of engine).

What the exemplars do (each releases freed pages outside the pause that ends marking):
- V8 (main 8bc5c682): freed pages go into a memory pool (MemoryAllocator::Free with kPool or
  kDelayThenPool, src/heap/memory-allocator.cc:368-407); a delayed task releases the pooled pages
  older than its epoch, 8 s after (memory_pool_timeout, src/flags/flag-definitions.h:2860-2867;
  MemoryPool::Config, src/heap/memory-pool.h:82-87; the task, src/heap/memory-pool.cc:446-529),
  on a worker thread, or with --single-threaded on the isolate's task runner between tasks
  (:504-510). A collection that reduces memory releases the pool at once
  (ReleasePooledChunksImmediately, src/heap/heap.cc:1118-1121), and memory pressure or a last
  resort releases everything (:1260-1268).
- SpiderMonkey (main 98bddef2): the GC's Decommit state decommits free arenas and chunks, on a
  helper thread, or without one on the main thread in that slice (GCRuntime::startDecommit,
  js/src/gc/GC.cpp:2302-2357; BackgroundDecommitTask, :2359-2390).
- JSC: bmalloc's scavenger thread returns free memory in the background (to cite at the pin).

A probe that pools every page beyond the cap (no release outside collections that reduce
memory; non-LTO, CPU 3): the same final pause, 14.6 ms with the release, is 4.1 ms (the engine's
sweep work 11.0 ms -> 0.66 ms); what is left is the sweep's freeing (2.45 ms) and the marking.

e50f5725 (p2-w6-s5-wip, an agent's; on main cccf7545), approved as planned (V8's pool):
1. With pacing, a collection no longer gives the spare pages beyond the cap back in its pause
   (Heap::trim_spare_pages): they stay in the spare pool, where allocation takes pages first, and
   count in the heap's committed memory only up to the cap (Heap::pool_cap, committed_bytes), so
   that pacing and the memory reducer see the heap as before.
2. A collection that reduces memory gives them back at once, as before and as V8's
   ReleasePooledChunksImmediately.
3. The others go back 8 s after the pool first passed the cap (POOL_TIMEOUT, V8's
   memory_pool_timeout), in the memory reducer's timer (Heap::release_pool from
   memory_reducer_timer), whose deadline (Engine::memory_reducer_deadline) names the pool's when
   it comes first; the reducer's own timer then runs at its own deadline alone (an earlier run
   would sample the allocation and could put the reducer off). A host that never runs the timer
   keeps the pages for reuse.
4. Without pacing (the unit tests, TRUST_JS_GC_PACING=0, the counts), collections give the pages
   back as they end, as before.
5. TRust's page actor runs the timer between tasks from the engine's deadline
   (trust_js_backend.rs:5108-5118, run_memory_reducer at 30051-30068: it shortens its wait to
   memory_reducer_deadline and calls run_memory_reducer when due), so the pool's deadline wakes
   it; the runtime's event loop does the same (trust-js-runtime's run_to_completion).
6. Tests: spare_pages_beyond_the_cap_wait_in_a_pool_for_the_reducers_timer (gc_core); the
   reducer's tests read the reducer's own deadline (MemoryReducer::deadline), the engine's being
   the pool's when it comes first. DIAGNOSTICS.md and the Engine's reducer API describe the pool.

### Compact baseline templates, step 2: equality and `!` (record, 2026-11-05)

7d0147a4 on p2-compact (from c50a0b4e, step 1 as landed; an agent's), landed on main as cbfa5881
over f3b8700c: the code is 7d0147a4's plus W6's steps 4 and 5 (2af3bfee..e50f5725), line for line,
and that combined tree's ARM64 lib suite passed (2,832 passed, 9 ignored) before main moved; the
design's item 3 ("Compact baseline
templates (census, survey and design, 2026-11-04)"). Scope as step 1: first-stage code outside
loops. A chunk now records whether it is a second-stage recompilation (Chunk::second_stage, set
when compile_with_inlines splices call sites), and jit::compact_templates is
use_shared_stub's rule (shared stubs on, the site not in a loop body) for a first-stage chunk
assembled by the chunk compiler. Second-stage code, loop bodies and a TRUST_JS_JIT_INLINE_STUBS
build keep today's templates, emit_eq_inline and emit_not_inline, byte for byte.

The compiler (all tiers):
1. A literal operand of an equality compiles on the right: `"{" === x` is `x; "{"; StrictEq`.
   A literal (a Number, signed or not, a String, a Boolean, null, undefined, or `!` or `void`
   of one; bytecode::literal_truthiness) has no effect, and IsStrictlyEqual and IsLooselyEqual
   are symmetric, the latter coercing only the operand that is not a literal, at most once,
   whichever side it is on; so evaluating the other operand first is unobservable.
   SpiderMonkey's emitter does the same for its constant operand (BytecodeEmitter.cpp,
   tryEmitConstantEq: the expression, then StrictConstantEq with the constant as an
   immediate), and V8's bytecode generator matches a literal undefined, null or Boolean on
   either side and visits only the other (BytecodeGenerator::VisitCompareOperation,
   IsLiteralCompareUndefined/Null, IsLiteralStrictCompareBoolean). Minified code puts the
   literal first (Djot's `"{"===t.subject.charAt(e)`: 158 of its 330 compiled equality sites).
2. `!` of a literal is its Boolean (`!0`, `!1`: minified true and false; 112 of Djot's 141
   compiled `!` sites), as V8's parser folds `!` of a literal (parser.cc,
   Parser::BuildUnaryExpression) and JSC's of a Number (ASTBuilder.h, createLogicalNot).
3. `void` of a literal is `undefined` (Op::Undef), as V8's and JSC's generators evaluate
   nothing for the literal (BytecodeGenerator::VisitVoid, VoidNode::emitBytecode).
4. `!` of an equality is the negated equality (`!(a == b)` is `a != b`, asm.js's way of writing
   it: Mandreel's and zlib's `if(!(r2 ==0))`): the same operands, the same comparison, its
   Boolean negated, as JSC compiles `!` in a condition by inverting the condition's branches
   (NodesCodegen.cpp, LogicalNotNode::emitBytecodeInConditionContext) and V8 by inverting the
   test's control flow (BytecodeGenerator::VisitNot). A numeric chain then takes the comparison
   and its branch in registers, as it took `a != b`.

The generated code (ARM64), at compact sites:
- An equality whose right operand is a constant (the operation before it pushes one, and the
  equality is no jump target; jit::EqConstant, emit_eq_constant) never pushes it, as JSC's
  Baseline specializes strict equality on a constant operand (JITOpcodes.cpp:642-765,
  compileOpStrictEq) and SpiderMonkey's Baseline its StrictConstantEq
  (BaselineCodeGen.cpp:3171-3232, emitConstantStrictEq):
  - strict, undefined, null or a Boolean: one compare of the operand's word;
  - a Number: FMOV and FCMP (FCMP #0.0 for zero), which every non-Number word fails as
    unordered: unequal for a strict comparison, the stub for a loose one;
  - loose, undefined or null: `tag | 2` against null's tag, and an Object's ic_plain byte
    (unequal unless the Object may be [[IsHTMLDDA]]), as V8's Sparkplug tests a loose nil
    comparison in line (baseline-compiler.cc, VisitTestUndetectable);
  - a String whose text the heap already has a canonical string for (the interned one-unit
    string of an ASCII unit, which charAt and indexing return, or the marked string of its
    existing key: an index's, a static name's, a heap atom's; Chunk::jit_const_canonical_str_word,
    which makes no atom): an identity test against that string, then the stub. A constant with
    no canonical string takes the stub with the constant pushed.
  The result drives a fused JumpIfFalse (also through a forwarding Jump), or replaces the
  operand by the Boolean. A region's equality whose right operand is the constant the operation
  before it pushed takes the same tests with both operands on the stack.
- Every other equality tests two Numbers in line (LDP, two FMOVs, FCMP: unordered for every
  other word, the canonical NaN included), as JSC's Baseline keeps its generic strict
  equality's int32 test in line (compileOpStrictEq), and otherwise is w1 = the site's pc and a
  call to the shared Equal stub for its (strict, negate) pair and result form, entered past its
  own load and Number test (emit_equal_site, emit_equal_call, emit_equal_stub; a strict call is
  two instructions, a loose one three, with the throw test, and a fused branch tests w9 with
  one CBZ). The stub does emit_eq_inline's work once per process: two Numbers by FCMP (for a
  constant's fallback, which enters at the top); one word one value
  but the canonical NaN; two Strings by their keys when both carry one (one key a text, Proxy
  step 2's lstr::KEY_MARK), else by length, else by content when both are flat buffers of one
  width and at most 64 bytes (the in-line template sent every equal-length pair to the helper);
  a strict pair of different tags, Objects, Symbols or Booleans unequal; a loose pair of
  undefined and null equal, and either unequal to anything else but a possible [[IsHTMLDDA]]
  Object. It calls the checked helper itself for the rest (H_STRICT_EQ, or H_EXEC for a loose
  comparison, then the explicit poll when the site's baseline call would end in one), with the
  pc the site passed, and returns the helper's flag for a loose one.
- `!` is w1 = the pc and a call to the shared Not stub (emit_not_site, emit_not_stub), which
  pushes the negated ToBoolean or, for a fused JumpIfFalse, returns it in w9 (one CBZ); a
  BigInt takes the generic helper from the stub, whose ToBoolean neither throws nor allocates.
  V8's Sparkplug calls ToBooleanForBaselineJump (VisitToBooleanLogicalNot), SpiderMonkey's
  Baseline its ToBool IC (emit_Not).
- A LoadLocal pair compared for a branch takes the two reads' templates and the compact
  equality, in place of the in-line pair template (emit_local_eq_branch) and of a numeric
  chain's speculation, as the pair template pre-empted the chain before. Every other numeric
  chain keeps its equality branches.

The first version (8a9224ca) differed in three ways that the counts showed wrong: it kept
numeric chains from taking equality branches at compact sites (Mandreel +0.68%, zlib +0.55%:
asm.js's `r13 == 0` in large loop bodies, which use_shared_stub treats as straight-line code,
lost its chain), it called the stub for two Numbers (React +0.54%: the reducer callbacks'
`todo.id === action.payload.id`, first-stage code that never gets a second stage, paid the call
and the veneer, four instructions of its own), and its constant form asked the assembler
whether each outcome label was referenced (a search of every patch so far: quadratic in a large
function's compile, 146 of the 31K instruction samples of a Mandreel run).

NOTES (for the steps after this one)

- Every call of a process-wide stub goes through the chunk's veneer, MOVZ/MOVK/MOVK and BR: four
  instructions on top of the BL and the RET, which first-stage code that never reaches a second
  stage pays at every compact site (React's +0.54% in the first version was mostly that). V8
  calls its builtins directly once it has remapped them into its code range (short builtin
  calls), and JSC and SpiderMonkey allocate all JIT code in one executable region within a
  branch's reach; here each chunk is mapped on its own. An LDR-literal veneer would halve the cost
  at the same 16 bytes; direct calls need the chunk's address before its branches are resolved.
- The optional region copies are 62% of Djot's first-stage machine code (998,288 of 1,611,520
  bytes), the baseline templates under them still emitted. The exemplars' baselines emit no
  optimized copies; their optimizing tiers come later, with feedback.
- After an equality, `&&` and `||` (JumpIfFalsePeek, JumpIfTruePeek: 190 and 193 bytes a site,
  167 and 89 sites in Djot) test the pushed Boolean through a ToBoolean template of their own.
- The exemplars intern every string literal; here a constant pool's String is its own cell and
  atoms are strong roots, so the constant forms test identity only against a canonical string
  the heap already has, and make no atom.

### Compact baseline templates, step 3: property writes and truthiness branches (record, 2026-11-05)

9c77c3fa on p2-compact (from 84bda962, step 2 as landed over W6's steps 4-5), the design's item 4
("Compact baseline templates (census, survey and design, 2026-11-04)") and, as the coordinator
asked after step 2, the short-circuit branch templates (`&&`, `||`: 190 and 193 bytes a site in
Djot).

Property writes (SetProp, SetPropDrop, SetPropThisDrop, SetPropLocalDrop, and the store of
AppendProp's `o.k += v`), as the reads of step 1: a store outside loops (use_shared_stub's rule)
whose cache was empty when its code was compiled (every way IC_EMPTY: every store of a function's
first native code, compiled at its first bytecode run; a site whose bytecode runs filled the
cache, at t1a2, keeps the in-line template, as a read with a way to bake does) keeps in line:
- the receiver's load (the operand, ctx.this_word or the local) and its object-tag test, the
  payload into x10;
- the cache's address in x8 and, for a store that may create its property (a name that is no
  index, `length` or `prototype`; store_may_create), the site's key word in x6 (an atom's address,
  which lives as long as the heap the code belongs to);
- the call of the shared stub, a branch on its answer, and the helper's stub call (emit_op_helper
  H_SET_PROP, whose stub tries a proven setter's direct call), as the in-line template's slow path.

The stub (jit::SharedStub::PropWrite, emit_prop_write_stub; one per receiver form (the operand
under the value, or `this` or a local), expression form (`keep`: the value replaces the receiver
operand) and creation) runs what every site carried: the expression form's test of its value (no
TDZ or property-only word as a result), the receiver's exotic kind and ic_plain byte, the ways
(four, x5 their count and x8 the cursor): an own-data update (the receiver shape, the slot under
the map's length; a filled way proves the property a writable data property) or a creation
transition (emit_prop_create_probe, now taking the key word from x6 in the stub: the receiver
shape, the prototype, the epoch, extensibility and no prototype flag, a small map with room,
the predicted layout's key or the transition's layout, and the record grown when the new slot
lacks room, keeping x5 too), the value's store, the write barrier's card mark (every commit, the
update's and the creation's), and for a creation the layout, the shape and the length; then the
operands' pops. It returns w9 = 1 when stored, 0 for the helper with nothing written.
Process-wide: the prototype epoch's address is a process static; the key word is the site's.

V8's Sparkplug calls a builtin for every named store with feedback (StoreICBaseline;
baseline-compiler.cc), SpiderMonkey's Baseline its site's IC stub (BaselineCodeGen.cpp,
emitNextIC), and JSC's Baseline runs the shared handler its data IC names
(JITPropertyAccess.cpp).

Truthiness branches: step 2's Not stub becomes a family of ToBoolean stubs (SharedStub::ToBoolean,
emit_to_boolean_stub; the Boolean in w1, the condition helper's register): `!` (the negated
Boolean in place of the operand), `!` feeding a JumpIfFalse (popped, negated), a short-circuit
branch (JumpIfFalsePeek, JumpIfTruePeek: the operand kept) and JumpIfFalse (popped). A BigInt, or
an Object that may be [[IsHTMLDDA]], takes the condition helper (COND_PEEK_TRUTHY) from the stub,
which neither throws nor allocates; so no site passes its pc. At compact sites a short-circuit
branch tests a Boolean in line (the word's XOR with PACK_BOOL is its payload, 0 or 1, for a
Boolean only) and calls the stub for any other value (emit_peek_cond_inline's compact form, which
regions share, their JumpIfFalse too), and JumpIfFalse keeps its in-line Boolean test and calls
the stub for any other value instead of the condition helper, as JSC's Baseline keeps op_jfalse's Boolean test in
line and calls a thunk for the rest (JITOpcodes.cpp, emit_op_jfalse, valueIsFalseyGenerator) and
V8's Sparkplug tests its static roots in line before calling ToBooleanForBaselineJump
(baseline-compiler.cc, JumpIfToBoolean). `??` (JumpIfNotNullishPeek) keeps its two compares.

### Compact baseline templates: the veneer as an LDR literal (record, 2026-11-05)

e34e863f on p2-compact (over step 3, 9c77c3fa), the coordinator's item (b) after step 2: every
call of a process-wide shared stub goes through its chunk's veneer (emit_shared_stubs), and that
veneer was MOVZ/MOVK/MOVK/BR x16, four instructions a call. It is now

    LDR x16, #8        (VENEER_LDR, 0x5800_0050)
    BR  x16            (VENEER_BR,  0xD61F_0200)
    .word lo, hi       (the stub's address, little-endian)

at the same 16 bytes, two instructions a call: the address is a literal the load reads from the
veneer itself, which W^X never writes after the chunk's publication. A stub with no process-wide
copy (a context unlike the first one, global_stub_address) is still emitted in its chunk, whose
sites call it with one BL. Asm::ldr_literal_x
emits the load (imm19 in words); skip_unused_callee_saved_fp's debug scan, which decodes every
word of a finished chunk, steps over the two literal words after a VENEER_LDR/VENEER_BR pair
(5d0dfa29, the first version, failed four lib tests in debug builds there: a literal word decoded
as a SIMD&FP instruction that bypassed Asm::emit_fp; amended as e34e863f). A test runs the
sequence (literal_load_reads_the_words_after_it: ldr x0, #8; ret; .quad).

V8's ARM64 builtin call is the same pair when its builtins are off the code range: kAbsolute
loads the builtin's absolute entry from a literal (Ldr scratch, Operand(BuiltinEntry(builtin),
RelocInfo::OFF_HEAP_TARGET)) and calls through the register, kPCRelative is one BL when the
builtins sit in the code range, kIndirect loads the entry from the isolate's table
(macro-assembler-arm64.cc, MacroAssembler::CallBuiltin, fetched 2026-11-05). No per-heap or
per-thread word is in the literal: the address is the process-wide stub's.

### Compact baseline templates: tier-up of hot first-stage code, measured before building (record, 2026-11-05)

The coordinator's item (c-tierup): today a chunk that reaches the inline checkpoint with an empty
plan stays first-stage forever; hot first-stage code would recompile once as a second stage,
with today's in-line templates and its caches seeded. Measured before building, on three probe
branches (not for landing):

- p2-tierup-probe, 42f32e46 (over 5d0dfa29, the veneer's first version): at the first
  checkpoint with an empty plan (about 100 runs), TRUST_JS_TIERUP=1 recompiles
  (compile_with_inlines with an empty plan, the second-stage flag set for a seeded recompile)
  and moves the call caches' epoch; 2 recompiles without the epoch (callers' filled caches keep
  the first-stage code, which stays valid); 3 moves the epoch alone; 0 is off.
- p2-tierup-probe2, f309b791 (over e34e863f): the same at the first checkpoint (empty plan or
  unchanged feedback) at or past TRUST_JS_TIERUP_AT runs (100, 500, 2100, 8500: the checkpoints).
- p2-tierup-probe3, 2c5b3943 (over f309b791): two second-stage fallbacks behind
  TRUST_JS_PROBE_FIX (below).

The epoch does not dominate: a one-time tier-up per hot function moves it 18-234 times, and its

WHY: THE SECOND STAGE IS WORSE THAN THE COMPACT FIRST STAGE AT SOME SITES

Helper tallies (TRUST_JS_JIT_OPSTAT, TRUST_JS_JIT_PROPSTAT, CALLSTAT; diag/), compile metrics
(TRUST_JS_PERF_METRICS) and profiles (prof/*-p3-*.data, instructions:u):

- Equality. Today's in-line template sends two Strings of one length to the helper; the compact
  site's Equal stub compares them (keys, length, content up to 64 bytes). PdfJS's tier-up code
  takes the helper 1,203,011 times for `==` against 332,166 (its `cmd == "..."` tests).
- A read whose cache was monomorphic when the recompile ran bakes that one state and sends a miss
  straight to the helper (jit_cache_preferred; emit_prop_load_inline's `compact` arm), even when a
  later shape is in the cache: PROPSTAT's "data cached (other template guard)". GBEmu: 13.1M such
  reads with no tier-up (its inlined second stages already have them), 15.1M with it (at 100
  runs, no epoch); DeltaBlue 9,180 and 36,403 (BinaryConstraint's `this.direction`, `this.v1`, `this.v2` over its two
  constraint classes). The first-stage code had no baked state (its caches were empty at its
  compile), so its stub probed every way.
- Operator chains (build_chain) bake their reads' states too, and a bail replays every remaining
  op of the chain through the generic helper (GBEmu's `parentObj.LCDTicks < k` chains: a
  GetPropLocal, a Const and a Lt in helpers each time).
- Compile cost: Djot's 37 recompiles add 9.6 ms of compile (jit 44.4 to 52.5 ms, bytecode 9.5 to
  11.0 ms), its +2.8% at 100 runs and +0.3% at 8500.
- EarleyBoyer's sc_Pair (step 3's cost): it tiers up, but today's in-line creation stores cost
  what the stub calls did (sc_Pair and Stub:PropWrite(create) 1,313 samples, 50K instructions
  each; sc_Pair 1,270 after the tier-up), so EarleyBoyer gains 0.13%.
- Not yet explained: chai (stringDistance, 17-23% of its instructions, costs the same in both
  stages; set_computed_element's named inserts with shape transitions appear only with the tier-up;
  its minor collections pause 25% longer at the same object counts), Splay (its string
  concatenation reaches jit_add_strings 2.4 times as often), RayTrace (+0.5% at 8500).

THE TWO FALLBACKS (p2-tierup-probe3)

TRUST_JS_PROBE_FIX bit 1: the in-line equality template's slow path calls the shared Equal stub
(emit_equal_call, the operands reloaded) instead of the helper, outside string accumulations; the
stub compares Strings and calls the helper for the rest. V8's Sparkplug calls its Equal and
StrictEqual builtins for every comparison it does not decide in line (baseline-compiler.cc,
VISIT_TYPED_COMPARE_OPERATION); JSC's Baseline calls operationCompareStrictEq after its constant
and Int32 fast paths (JITOpcodes.cpp, compileOpStrictEq).

Bit 2: a baked monomorphic read's miss probes the live ways through the shared way loop
(Stub:PropWays), as a polymorphic site's last baked miss already does, before the helper. JSC's
Baseline loads its site's data IC and runs its handler, which covers every case the cache holds,
the slow path only after all of them (JITPropertyAccess.cpp, emit_op_get_by_id,
generateDataICFastPath); SpiderMonkey's Baseline stubs end every failure path in
EmitStubGuardFailure, the jump to the chain's next stub and at last its fallback
(BaselineCacheIRCompiler.cpp, BaselineCacheIRCompiler::compile).

Helper traffic, no tier-up (diag/p3fix0-*, p3fix3-*): GBEmu's "other template guard" reads 13.1M
to 4.6M (the rest are chains), PdfJS's `==` helper calls 332,166 to 33,464, DeltaBlue's guard
misses 9,180 to 25.

The fallbacks alone take every workload below main, GBEmu by 9.9% and PdfJS by 2.9%: its

still costs chai +0.66%, Splay +0.66%, RayTrace +0.53%, DeltaBlue +0.24% and Djot +0.31% on top
of them at 8500 (React -4.7%, TypeScript -1.6%, RegExp -0.9% are its gains), so against main
Splay (+0.43%) and RayTrace (+0.27%) stay past the 0.2% bound. RayTrace's tier-ups include its
Class.create constructor (`function() { this.initialize.apply(this, arguments); }`), and
construct_arguments_apply_forwarder takes 8% more instructions after it (prof/rt-p3-m*.data).

Each fallback alone, without tier-up (counts/probe3-f1m0.txt, f2m0.txt), against FIX=0: bit 1
PdfJS -2.40%, Djot -0.62%, Vue -0.61%, EarleyBoyer -0.50%, React -0.26%, no workload above

and Richards +0.08%, Djot +0.07%, RayTrace +0.04% (the larger code at monomorphic sites).

Code bytes (bytes-p3/): bit 1 Djot -1,540 (-0.05%), React -348, Vue -140; bit 2 Djot +29,960
(+1.05%), React +1,536, Vue +3,376 (a way-loop call after each baked monomorphic read: MOV of the
cache's address, BL, and the status's three tests); both Djot +28,420 (+1.0%). The miss could
call step 1's PropRead stub instead (its way loop, landings and commit; MOV, BL, CBNZ), about
half the bytes.


WHAT FOLLOWS

- Step 3 and the veneer meet the step's exit as a series against main without the tier-up: all
  nineteen workloads run fewer instructions (impl-veneer-record-draft.txt).
- The two fallbacks, as their own commits against main: today's templates (second stages, loop
  bodies), not the first stage's. The read's miss would call step 1's PropRead stub (way loop,
  landings, commit) rather than PropWays with the template's landings, for about half the bytes.
- The tier-up after them, still at the last checkpoint (8500 runs: the fewest recompiles and no
  later inline plan lost), once its remaining costs are understood: Splay (+0.66% on top of the
  fallbacks; its string concatenation), chai (+0.66%; computed named inserts, minor pauses),
  RayTrace (+0.53%; the arguments-apply forwarder after its constructor tiers up), and the
  chains' bails, which replay their ops through helpers after a baked read misses. Those need a
  way back from a failed speculation: JSC counts its optimized code's OSR exits and reoptimizes
  past a threshold (CodeBlock.cpp, shouldReoptimizeNow, exitCountThresholdForReoptimization,
  doubled per retry); a chain would count its bails and its chunk recompile once without the
  stale state. A design note first.


### Today's in-line templates: two slow paths through shared stubs (record, 2026-11-05)

The coordinator's item (B), from the tier-up measurement: two weaknesses of today's in-line
templates (second stages, loop bodies) that the compact first stage does not share, each its
own commit on p2-fallbacks, from main ce9a19e3:

- cb2bf331, the equality's slow path. emit_eq_inline decides Numbers, nullish operands,
  Booleans, identities and Strings of different lengths in line and sent the rest to the
  checked helper: two Strings of one length, BigInts, loose coercions. Its slow path now calls
  step 2's shared Equal stub (emit_equal_call, the operands reloaded from the stack: x12 and
  x13 hold payloads on some of the template's paths), which compares two Strings by their keys
  or, flat and of one width, their contents up to 64 bytes, and calls the helper itself for the
  rest; where the compiler emits no shared stubs, and at a string accumulation's start, the
  helper stays. V8's Sparkplug calls its compare builtins for what it does not decide in line
  (baseline-compiler.cc, VISIT_TYPED_COMPARE_OPERATION); JSC's Baseline calls
  operationCompareStrictEq after its constant and Int32 paths (JITOpcodes.cpp,
  compileOpStrictEq).
- 879082db, a baked read's miss. A named read whose cache held one shape when its code was
  made (a second stage's seeded caches, code compiled after bytecode runs warmed them) bakes
  that state (jit_cache_preferred), and its miss went straight to the checked helper even when
  the cache had since taken the receiver's shape (PROPSTAT's "data cached (other template
  guard)"). The miss now calls step 1's PropRead stub (x8 the cache; x9 and x10 the receiver as
  a compact site leaves them; the way loop, the landings and the commit), and only a miss there
  takes the helper: MOV, BL, CBNZ and B at the site, as the coordinator asked rather than the
  probe's PropWays call with the template's landings. A key-checked way (an Array holder) stays
  the helper's, the stub carrying no key word; a polymorphic site's baked probes keep their way
  loop. JSC's Baseline runs its site's data IC handler over every case the cache holds before
  its slow path (JITPropertyAccess.cpp, emit_op_get_by_id, generateDataICFastPath);
  SpiderMonkey's Baseline stubs end each failure path in the jump to the chain's next stub
  (BaselineCacheIRCompiler.cpp, EmitStubGuardFailure).

Tests: jit::compact_equality_tests::equality_in_loops_agrees_with_the_tree_walker (equality in
loop bodies over pairs of one length: equal and unequal contents, flat and view, one- and
two-byte, keyed, past 64 bytes, BigInts, coercions; values, branches, negated branches,
constants, a throwing coercion; against the tree-walker), which fails with the stub call's
negate flipped; jit::baked_read_tests (each read form warmed on one receiver class on the
bytecode VM, then read on two more: one checked read a class, the rest native), which fails
without 879082db (30 checked reads for 30).
